quote: per FDA Guidance on Formal Meetings Between CDER and Sponsors (2017)
error: This cites the December 2017 draft, whose actual title was 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products'. That draft was replaced by the September 2023 PDUFA VII revised draft of the same title. The 2023 draft added Type D and INTERACT meetings, so the 2017 document is no longer current, and its title is quoted wrongly too.
correct: FDA draft guidance 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products' (September 2023, PDUFA VII), which covers Type A, B, B(EOP), C, D and INTERACT meetings.

quote: Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition in Clinical Investigations (2024)
error: The final guidance was issued in December 2023 (the draft came out in December 2021), so the year is wrong.
correct: FDA Guidance: Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition in Clinical Investigations (final, December 2023).

quote: specify the design per FDA Guidance on Oncology Dose Optimization (2023)
error: 2023 is the year of the draft (January 2023). FDA finalized 'Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases' in August 2024, so the current document is the 2024 final.
correct: FDA Guidance: Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases (final, August 2024).

quote: reference: 'ICH E9 Section 2.2.5 — Multiplicity'
error: ICH E9 Section 2.2.5 is 'Multiple Primary Variables'. It is not a general multiplicity section and it does not cover pairwise comparisons across multiple treatment arms. Adjusting for multiple comparisons, such as multiple arms, is covered in ICH E9 Section 5.6, 'Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels'.
correct: ICH E9 Section 5.6 (Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels) for multiple-arm and pairwise multiplicity; Section 2.2.5 covers multiple primary variables only.

quote: ICH E9 Section 3.3 requires each arm to be adequately powered if formal pairwise comparisons are planned.
error: ICH E9 Section 3.3 is 'Type of Comparison' (superiority, equivalence/non-inferiority, dose-response). It sets no requirement about powering each arm. Sample size is covered in Section 3.5.
correct: Sample size and power considerations are in ICH E9 Section 3.5 (Sample Size). Section 3.3 covers the type of comparison.

quote: ICH E8(R1) Section 4 recommends the title convey the intervention, condition, phase, and design.
error: ICH E8(R1) Section 4 is 'Drug Development Planning'. Nothing in E8(R1) recommends what a protocol title should contain, so this attribution is invented.
correct: Content of the protocol title page comes from ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 Appendix B (and ICH M11 for structured protocols), not ICH E8(R1) Section 4.

quote: EMA requires an EU Risk Management Plan per Directive 2001/83/EC Article 104a.
error: Article 104a is a transitional provision. It lets authorities impose a risk management system on products authorised before 21 July 2012. The general obligation to submit an RMP and operate a risk management system is in Article 8(3)(iaa) and Article 104(3)(c), and in Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 for centrally authorised products.
correct: EU RMP: Directive 2001/83/EC Article 8(3)(iaa) and Article 104(3)(c) (and Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 for centrally authorised products); GVP Module V.

quote: Per ICH E2A and FDA Guidance on Safety Reporting (2015)
error: The 2015 FDA document, 'Safety Assessment for IND Safety Reporting', was only ever a draft. It was replaced by the June 2021 draft 'Sponsor Responsibilities — Safety Reporting Requirements and Safety Assessment for IND and Bioavailability/Bioequivalence Studies'. Citing it as current FDA guidance misstates both its status and whether it is still in effect.
correct: FDA draft guidance 'Sponsor Responsibilities — Safety Reporting Requirements and Safety Assessment for IND and BA/BE Studies' (June 2021), with the final 2012 guidance 'Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies'.

quote: ICH E14 requires QTc assessment for all new molecular entities. Failing to assess cardiac safety may result in a clinical hold or Refuse to File.
error: ICH E14 does not require QTc assessment for every NME. It applies to new drugs with systemic bioavailability, and the guideline itself notes that a dedicated QT study is often not needed for large proteins and monoclonal antibodies. The same overstatement appears in the helpText at line 1338 ('QTc assessment is required for all new molecular entities'). The finding is also rated 'critical'.
correct: ICH E14, as updated by the E14/S7B Q&As, recommends evaluating QT/QTc prolongation for new drugs with systemic bioavailability, through a TQT study or concentration-QTc modelling. A sponsor can justify a different approach, for example for large-molecule biologics with low risk of direct ion-channel interaction.

quote: FDORA Section 3601 (explained in FDA draft guidance on Diversity Action Plans, June 2024) requires Phase 3 and pivotal trials to submit a Diversity Action Plan. Sponsors must provide justification if a plan is not submitted.
error: This states the Diversity Action Plan obligation as currently binding. Under FD&C Act 505(z) and 520(g)(9), the requirement applies only to studies whose enrollment begins 180 days or more after FDA publishes FINAL guidance. The file itself cites only the June 2024 draft, and line 2195 says this correctly. The helpText at line 2203 ('Diversity Action Plans are required for Phase 3 and other pivotal studies unless an exemption is granted') repeats the error.
correct: Diversity Action Plans will be required for Phase 3 and other pivotal studies (and certain device studies) whose enrollment begins 180 days or more after FDA issues final DAP guidance. Until then, submitting one is voluntary and recommended.

quote: Per FDA Guidance on Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition in Clinical Investigations (2024)
error: Wrong date. FDA finalized this guidance in December 2023; the draft was December 2021.
correct: FDA Guidance: Digital Health Technologies for Remote Data Acquisition in Clinical Investigations (final, December 2023).

quote: specify the design per FDA Guidance on Oncology Dose Optimization (2023).
error: 2023 is the date of the draft. FDA finalized 'Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases' in August 2024, so the citation points to a superseded draft.
correct: FDA Guidance: Optimizing the Dosage of Human Prescription Drugs and Biological Products for the Treatment of Oncologic Diseases (final, August 2024).

quote: Trials exceeding 5,000 subjects require robust safety monitoring infrastructure, centralized statistical monitoring, and potentially a larger DSMB per FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial DSMBs (2006).
error: The 2006 FDA DMC guidance sets no 5,000-subject threshold and does not require centralized statistical monitoring or a larger DMC for big trials. The requirement is attributed to a source that does not contain it.
correct: The 2006 FDA guidance (Establishment and Operation of Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees) discusses when a DMC is advisable: large, multicenter or long trials with mortality or major morbidity endpoints. It sets no enrollment-size threshold or associated requirements.

quote: 'ICH E3, Section 10; 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(ii); FDA Guidance on Diversity (2020)'
error: ICH E3 Section 10 is 'Study Patients' (10.1 Disposition, 10.2 Protocol Deviations). It does not cover demographics or baseline characteristics. The question at line 998 and the reference at line 1017 cite it for demographics, baseline characteristics and eligibility criteria.
correct: Demographics and baseline characteristics are in ICH E3 Section 11.2 ('Demographic and Other Baseline Characteristics'). Eligibility criteria are in Section 9.3 ('Selection of Study Population').

quote: 'ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands; NRC Report (2010); FDA Guidance on Missing Data (2020)'
error: FDA has issued no general 'Guidance on Missing Data (2020)'. Line 755 cites the same non-existent document ('FDA Guidance (2020)'). Line 763 also credits FDA with a 10% discontinuation threshold ('FDA considers this a significant omission, particularly for trials with discontinuation rates above 10%') that no FDA document sets.
correct: The applicable sources are the 2010 NRC report 'The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials' (commissioned by FDA), ICH E9(R1) (adopted by FDA in 2021) and, for the EU, EMA/CPMP/EWP/1776/99 Rev. 1. No FDA discontinuation-rate threshold exists.

quote: 'Interim analyses must be overseen by an independent DMC operating under a ' +
error: This presents a requirement that does not exist. ICH E9 Section 4.5 asks that interim analyses be pre-planned with procedures that preserve Type I error and confidentiality. It does not require every interim analysis to be overseen by an independent DMC, and it does not require an alpha-spending function specifically (fixed group-sequential boundaries are also acceptable). The question at line 682 makes the same claim and attributes it to E9 4.5.
correct: ICH E9 4.5/4.6 and FDA's 2006 DMC guidance recommend independent DMCs for many trials with interim efficacy or safety looks. Interim analyses must be pre-specified with a method that controls Type I error (group-sequential boundaries or an alpha-spending function). DMC oversight is a recommendation, not a universal requirement.

quote: recommends DMCs for controlled trials intended to support marketing applications.
error: This misstates the 2006 FDA DMC guidance. The guidance says most clinical trials do not need a DMC. It recommends one mainly for large, randomized, multicenter trials of treatments meant to prolong life or reduce the risk of major adverse health outcomes, and for some other high-risk settings. It does not recommend DMCs for all controlled trials that support marketing applications. Line 334 says the same thing ('FDA strongly recommends independent data monitoring for pivotal studies').
correct: FDA's 2006 guidance 'Establishment and Operation of Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees' recommends DMCs for controlled trials with mortality or major-morbidity endpoints, for vulnerable populations or high-risk interventions, and for large multicenter studies of that kind. It states that many trials, including some pivotal trials, do not need one.

quote: FDA Guidance for Industry: Phase 1 Investigations (2015)
error: No FDA guidance with the title 'Phase 1 Investigations' was issued in 2015. The citation appears to be fabricated.
correct: The relevant FDA documents include 'Content and Format of Investigational New Drug Applications (INDs) for Phase 1 Studies of Drugs, Including Well-Characterized, Therapeutic, Biotechnology-derived Products' (1995), 'Estimating the Maximum Safe Starting Dose in Initial Clinical Trials for Therapeutics in Adult Healthy Volunteers' (2005) and 'CGMP for Phase 1 Investigational Drugs' (2008). Phase 1 is defined in 21 CFR 312.21(a).

quote: 'Every confirmatory trial must designate a single primary endpoint that is clinically ' +
error: ICH E9 does not require a single primary endpoint. Section 2.2.2 says there should 'generally' be only one primary variable, and Section 2.2.5 explicitly allows multiple primary variables with suitable Type I error control. FDA's Multiple Endpoints guidance (2022) covers co-primary and multiple primary endpoints. The question at line 342 makes the same claim.
correct: ICH E9 recommends generally one primary variable. Multiple or co-primary endpoints are acceptable when pre-specified with appropriate multiplicity control (ICH E9 2.2.2 and 2.2.5; FDA Multiple Endpoints in Clinical Trials, 2022).

quote: 'The FDA benefit-risk framework (PDUFA VI) requires explicit weighing of ' +
error: FDA's structured Benefit-Risk Framework was introduced under PDUFA V (the 2013 implementation plan). PDUFA VI continued it but did not create it. Neither one, nor ICH E3, requires an individual CSR to contain a structured benefit-risk assessment when deaths occur. The framework governs FDA's own review and the marketing-application benefit-risk summary (CTD 2.5.6). The same claims appear at lines 943 and 946.
correct: The FDA Benefit-Risk Framework dates from PDUFA V and was carried forward in PDUFA VI and VII. A benefit-risk discussion belongs in the marketing application (21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(viii); CTD Module 2.5.6), not as a mandatory part of a CSR. ICH E3 12.3 requires death narratives and analysis, not a structured benefit-risk assessment.

quote: 'the primary assumption (e.g., MAR, MNAR), the analytical method, and at least ' +
error: No regulation or guidance requires 'at least two sensitivity analyses under alternative assumptions'. The number is invented and presented as a requirement.
correct: ICH E9(R1) asks for pre-specified sensitivity analyses that test the robustness of the main estimator's assumptions. It does not set a minimum number.

quote: 'Describe: (1) the estimand (treatment policy, composite, hypothetical, or ' +
error: Treatment policy, composite, hypothetical and principal stratum are not estimands. They are ICH E9(R1) strategies for handling intercurrent events. The list also leaves out the fifth strategy, while-on-treatment.
correct: ICH E9(R1) defines an estimand by five attributes: treatment, population, variable, intercurrent-event handling and population-level summary. It names five intercurrent-event strategies: treatment policy, hypothetical, composite variable, while on treatment, and principal stratum.

quote: The study phase must be declared per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv) to allow FDA to assess developmental appropriateness.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv) is the Form FDA 1571 commitment that an IRB complying with Part 56 will review and approve the study. It does not cover the study phase. The same wrong paragraph is repeated in the reference string at line 287.
correct: The requirement to identify the phase or phases of the clinical investigation is in 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(ii).

quote: 'ICH E8(R1) Section 3.1.3.1; FDA Guidance for Industry: Phase 1 Investigations (2015)'
error: ICH E8(R1) has no Section 3.1.3.1. Its Section 3 is 'Designing Quality into Clinical Studies'. Section 3.1.3.1 (Phase I) existed only in the original 1997 ICH E8, which E8(R1) replaced. Line 180 cites that superseded 'ICH E8 Section 3.1.3.1' as current.
correct: Cite ICH E8(R1) Section 4.3 (Clinical studies: human pharmacology, exploratory, confirmatory, post-approval) and its Annex on types of studies.

quote: 'ICH E9 Section 3.1.2; ICH E10 Section 2.6.1'
error: ICH E10 has no Section 2.6.1. Section 2 ends at 2.5 (External Control). Line 660 makes the same claim: 'ICH E10 Section 2.6.1 discusses comparator selection considerations.'
correct: Choice of comparator is covered in ICH E10 Section 2.4 (Active (Positive) Concurrent Control) and Section 3 (Choosing the Concurrent Control).

quote: '21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv); ICH E8(R1) Section 3'
error: ICH E8(R1) Section 3 is 'Designing Quality into Clinical Studies' (quality by design and critical-to-quality factors). It does not cover development phases or whether a study suits its stage of development.
correct: Development stages and study types are covered in ICH E8(R1) Section 4 (Drug Development Planning), Section 4.3 in particular.

quote: 'ICH E9 Section 2.3.2; FDA Guidance: Adaptive Designs (2019) Section IV.A'
error: Section IV.A of FDA's 2019 'Adaptive Designs for Clinical Drug and Biological Products' covers controlling the chance of erroneous conclusions (Type I error). It does not cover stratified randomization.
correct: For stratified randomization, cite ICH E9 Section 2.3.2 alone. Drop the Adaptive Designs Section IV.A reference.

quote: Per FDAAA 2007 (Section 505-1), REMS may be required
error: Section 505-1 is a section of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, not of FDAAA. FDAAA (Pub. L. 110-85) Title IX, section 901, added section 505-1 to the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355-1). FDAAA has no section 505-1.
correct: Per FD&C Act section 505-1 (21 U.S.C. 355-1), added by FDAAA 2007 section 901, FDA may require a REMS if it determines one is necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks.

quote: Per ICH E9 Section 5.5, the primary analysis should be fully pre-specified in the statistical analysis plan (SAP).
error: ICH E9 Section 5.5 is 'Estimation, Confidence Intervals and Hypothesis Testing'. Pre-specifying the analysis in the SAP is covered in Section 5.1, 'Prespecification of the Analysis'.
correct: Per ICH E9 Section 5.1 (Prespecification of the Analysis), the primary analysis should be pre-specified in the protocol/statistical analysis plan.

quote: while the PP population is preferred for non-inferiority and equivalence trials
error: ICH E9 (Section 5.2.3) does not say the per-protocol set is preferred for equivalence or non-inferiority trials. It says only that using the full analysis set in those trials is generally not conservative, and that its role should be considered carefully. Both analyses are expected, and conclusions should be robust across them (FDA's 2016 non-inferiority guidance says the same).
correct: Per ICH E9 Section 5.2.3, the full analysis set is generally primary for superiority trials. In equivalence and non-inferiority trials, the full analysis set is not conservative, so both the FAS and the PP analyses should be presented and the conclusions should hold under both.

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies" (2012), AESIs should be defined in the protocol and monitored via Standardized MedDRA Queries (SMQs) or Customized MedDRA Queries (CMQs).
error: This is a misattribution. The 2012 FDA final guidance on IND/BA-BE safety reporting covers 21 CFR 312.32/320.31 expedited reporting: definitions, causality, the 15-day and 7-day clocks, and aggregate analysis. It does not require AESIs to be defined in the protocol, and it does not tell sponsors to monitor them with SMQs or CMQs.
correct: Defining AESIs in the protocol and searching for them with SMQs or CMQs is industry practice that draws on CIOMS VI and MedDRA guidance. The 2012 FDA safety reporting guidance does not require it.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.31 (Amendments to an IND), amendments must describe the nature and significance of each change.
error: 21 CFR 312.31 is titled "Information amendments". It does not cover IND amendments in general. Protocol amendments are a separate section, 312.30, and no CFR section is titled "Amendments to an IND".
correct: 21 CFR 312.31 (Information amendments). IND amendments as a whole fall under 21 CFR 312.30 (protocol amendments) and 312.31 (information amendments).

quote: Information amendments (21 CFR 312.31(b)) cover all other changes.
error: The scope rule (essential information not covered by a protocol amendment, an IND safety report or the annual report) is in 312.31(a), 'Requirement for information amendment'. 312.31(b) covers only the content and format of an information amendment.
correct: Information amendments (21 CFR 312.31(a)) cover essential information not within the scope of a protocol amendment, IND safety report or annual report.

quote: { value: 'planned', label: 'Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Table 3' }
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 lists the nonclinical studies recommended for exploratory clinical trials (Section 7, approaches 1–5). It says nothing about when reproductive or embryo-fetal development studies are due. That timing is set out in the text of Section 11.
correct: Timing per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies).

quote: requires embryo-fetal development (EFD) studies to be completed per ICH M3(R2) Table 3
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 covers the nonclinical studies recommended for exploratory clinical trials. The rules on when EFD studies are needed before enrolling WOCBP are in Section 11 (11.3), not in a table.
correct: EFD studies completed per ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction Toxicity Studies).

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7), the IND must include a description of the drug substance and drug product, including the name, chemical structure, mechanism of action, route of administration, and proposed indication.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) is the chemistry, manufacturing and controls section. Route of administration, pharmacological class and broad objectives belong to the introductory statement, 312.23(a)(3). Mechanism of action belongs to pharmacology, 312.23(a)(8)(i). Neither is an (a)(7) requirement.
correct: Name, structure, pharmacological class, formulation, route and objectives go in the introductory statement (21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)(i)). Mechanism of action goes under 312.23(a)(8)(i). Drug substance and drug product CMC goes under 312.23(a)(7).

quote: FDA Guidance "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (2017)
error: The December 2017 draft was replaced by the September 2023 revised guidance of the same title, issued under PDUFA VII. That revision added Type D and INTERACT meetings. Citing the 2017 version as current refers to a superseded document.
correct: FDA Guidance "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (September 2023 revision), which describes Type A, B, B (EOP), C, D and INTERACT meetings.

quote: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, Office of New Drugs / CDER',
error: CDER's 2019 reorganisation of the Office of New Drugs ended the 'Division of Oncology Products 1'. Oncology review now sits in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, in the Divisions of Oncology 1, 2 and 3 and the hematology divisions.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER

quote: adds 45 days of FDA review for protocol agreement
error: An SPA does not add time to the IND's 30-day review. It is a separate request, usually made for a Phase 3 protocol after the IND is already in effect, and its 45-day response clock runs on its own without delaying when the IND takes effect. Line 1253 repeats the same claim: 'A Special Protocol Assessment adds 45 days to the FDA review timeline.'
correct: FDA aims to answer an SPA request within 45 days under the PDUFA goals. The request is separate from the 21 CFR 312.40 30-day IND review and does not lengthen it.

quote: FDA agreement is binding unless the sponsor fails to follow the agreed-upon protocol.
error: The exceptions to an SPA agreement are incomplete. Under FD&C Act 505(b)(5)(C), FDA can also change the agreement with the sponsor's written agreement, or when a substantial scientific issue essential to judging safety or effectiveness is identified after testing has begun. Under the SPA guidance, it can also do so when the data the sponsor relied on prove false, misleading or materially incomplete.
correct: An SPA agreement binds the review division. It can change if the sponsor agrees in writing, if a substantial scientific issue essential to safety or effectiveness is identified after testing begins, if the sponsor does not follow the agreed protocol, or if the data it relied on prove false or incomplete.

quote: "Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products" (2017)
error: The 2017 document was a draft guidance. FDA replaced it with a final guidance of the same title in September 2023 under PDUFA VII. The final guidance added Type D and INTERACT meetings to Types A, B, B(EOP) and C.
correct: Cite FDA Guidance 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products' (final, September 2023). Pre-IND meetings remain Type B.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) requires stability data at submission.
error: ICH Q1A(R2) sets the stability data package for registration (marketing) applications. It does not set IND stability requirements. IND stability content comes from 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a)-(b) and FDA's IND CMC guidances (Phase 1 guidance of 1995; Phase 2/3 guidance of 2003): stability data adequate to cover the duration of the planned trial. The guidance at line 1411 makes the same misattribution: 'A minimum of 1-2 months accelerated data ... per ICH Q1A(R2)'.
correct: Under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7) and FDA's IND CMC guidances, the IND must describe the stability program and give data showing the material stays within specification for the duration of the clinical study. ICH Q1A(R2) governs registration stability packages.

quote: Not yet — typically required before Phase 3 / NDA
error: Under ICH M3(R2) Section 8, carcinogenicity studies, when needed, are normally completed for marketing approval. They are not needed before large-scale clinical trials (Phase 3) unless there is a special concern. 'Before Phase 3' is wrong.
correct: When needed, carcinogenicity studies are typically completed before the marketing application (NDA/BLA). Phase 3 can proceed without them unless there is a specific cause for concern.

quote: Planned — timing per ICH M3(R2) Table 3
error: ICH M3(R2) Table 3 covers recommended nonclinical studies for exploratory clinical trials. Reproductive toxicity timing relative to enrolling WOCBP is set out in M3(R2) Section 11, not in a table. The finding at line 2000 makes the same miscitation: 'EFD studies to be completed per ICH M3(R2) Table 3'.
correct: Reproductive and developmental toxicity timing is given in ICH M3(R2) Section 11 (Reproduction toxicity studies, 11.3 Women of childbearing potential).

quote: FDA requires all drug product sponsors to complete a nitrosamine impurity risk assessment per the current FDA guidance
error: The FDA nitrosamine guidance (Rev. 2, September 2024) is non-binding. Its recommendations are addressed to manufacturers and applicants of marketed products and of pending or approved NDAs, ANDAs and BLAs. It does not impose a requirement that IND sponsors complete the assessment before IND submission. The help text at line 1822 says the same: 'all sponsors must conduct a risk assessment'.
correct: FDA recommends (non-binding guidance) that manufacturers of APIs and drug products, chiefly for marketed products and marketing applications, assess and control nitrosamine risk. For an IND it is good practice to assess the risk early, but it is not a regulatory requirement for submission.

quote: a dedicated study is recommended when renal clearance accounts for ≥30% of total clearance or the drug has a narrow therapeutic index
error: FDA's renal impairment guidance has no 30% renal-clearance cut-off. It recommends characterising PK in renal impairment for most drugs intended for patients who may have impaired renal function, including drugs eliminated mainly by non-renal routes, because renal impairment also changes metabolism and transport. A reduced design is an option, not an exemption below 30%. The option 'Not needed — minimal renal elimination (<30%)' at line 1933 relies on the same false threshold.
correct: FDA recommends a renal impairment PK study for most drugs likely to be used in patients with renal impairment, whatever the main elimination route. A reduced or staged design is possible for drugs that are not mainly renally eliminated.

quote: single-enantiomer development is generally preferred. A racemate requires justification.
error: FDA's 1992 Policy Statement for the Development of New Stereoisomeric Drugs states no preference for single enantiomers. It leaves the choice of racemate or single enantiomer to the sponsor and asks for stereochemistry-specific characterisation and controls either way.
correct: Under the 1992 FDA policy the sponsor may develop either a racemate or a single enantiomer. Either way, the stereoisomeric composition must be characterised and controlled, and the individual enantiomers' pharmacology and PK assessed.

quote: Dun & Bradstreet number required for FDA submissions per OMB guidance.
error: Form FDA 1571 and 21 CFR 312.23 do not require a DUNS number for an IND. The OMB DUNS requirement applied to federal grants and awards, and the federal government replaced DUNS with the SAM Unique Entity ID in April 2022. FDA uses DUNS for establishment registration and listing, not IND submission.
correct: An IND does not require a DUNS number. DUNS or FEI numbers apply to establishment registration and listing and to some application forms, not to Form FDA 1571.

quote: e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, Office of New Drugs / CDER
error: CDER reorganised the Office of New Drugs in 2019-2020, and 'Division of Oncology Products 1' no longer exists. Oncology review now sits in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, under Divisions of Oncology 1, 2 and 3 and the hematologic malignancies divisions.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, Office of New Drugs / CDER.

quote: ICH E1 provides guidance on the size of the safety database needed to support different phases of clinical development.
error: ICH E1 does not cover the safety database for each phase of development. It sets the total population exposure expected at marketing approval for drugs meant for long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions: about 1500 subjects in total, 300-600 treated for 6 months, and 100 treated for 1 year. The question at line 657 makes the same claim when it asks whether the database is adequate 'to support the proposed phase of development per ICH E1'.
correct: ICH E1 (Extent of Population Exposure to Assess Clinical Safety for Drugs Intended for Long-Term Treatment of Non-Life-Threatening Conditions) sets the expected exposure at marketing approval. Phase-appropriate nonclinical support for each clinical phase comes from ICH M3(R2). Phase-by-phase clinical safety data needs are not defined by E1.

quote: ICH M3(R2) Section 3; ICH S6(R1) Section 2; 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8)
error: This citation is offered for selecting pharmacologically relevant toxicology species. ICH M3(R2) Section 3 is 'Toxicokinetic and Pharmacokinetic Studies', not species selection.
correct: M3(R2) covers species for general toxicity studies under Repeated-Dose Toxicity Studies (Section 5) and its general principles (Section 1). For biologics, species selection is ICH S6(R1) (the addendum's Section 2, Species Selection).

quote: ICH M3(R2) Section 4; 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8); FDA Guidance: Content and Format of INDs for Phase 1 Studies
error: This is cited for the overall requirement that nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies be complete before first-in-human dosing. ICH M3(R2) Section 4 is 'Acute Toxicity Studies'.
correct: The general principles and timing of nonclinical studies relative to clinical trials are in M3(R2) Section 1 (General Principles), Section 5 (Repeated-Dose Toxicity, Table 1) and the guideline as a whole. Section 4 covers acute toxicity only.

quote: ICH E3 Section 12.2.2 requires that individual serious case narratives be interpretable in the context of the overall safety summary.
error: ICH E3 Section 12.2.2 is 'Display of Adverse Events', the summary tables of adverse events. Narratives of deaths, other serious adverse events and other significant adverse events are in Section 12.3.2. The reference string at line 716 ('ICH E3 Section 12.2.2') repeats the error.
correct: Individual narratives are covered by ICH E3 Section 12.3.2. Section 12.3.3 covers the analysis and discussion of deaths and serious events in the context of the overall safety data.

quote: ICH E2D Section III.B requires sponsors to make reasonable efforts to obtain follow-up information on serious cases.
error: ICH E2D uses Arabic section numbers (1-5) and has no Section III.B. Follow-up information is in Section 5.4 (Good Case Management Practices). E2D is also the post-approval ICSR guideline, not the clinical-trial one. The same nonexistent numbering appears in other E2D references in this file ('Section III', 'III.A', 'II.B', 'II.C', 'IV').
correct: ICH E2D Section 5.4 (Follow-up Information) covers follow-up of post-approval ICSRs. For a clinical-trial case under an IND, cite 21 CFR 312.32(d).

quote: ICH E6(R3) Appendix B; ICH E6(R3) Annex 1 §2.11; ICH E2A Section III.D; 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iv)
error: 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iv) is the IND safety-report trigger for a clinically important increase in the rate of serious suspected adverse reactions over the rate in the protocol or Investigator's Brochure. It says nothing about unblinding or emergency unblinding procedures, so it is cited here for something it does not contain.
correct: Unblinding of individual SUSAR cases is covered by ICH E2A Section III.D. For a US IND it is covered by FDA's 2010 final rule preamble and the guidance 'Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies' (2012), not by 312.32(c)(1)(iv). Remove the 312.32(c)(1)(iv) citation or replace it.

quote: Per 21 USC 355-1(g), REMS assessments must be submitted at 18 months, 3 years, and 7 years after initial REMS approval
error: The 18-month / 3-year / 7th-year assessment timetable is in section 505-1(d) (21 USC 355-1(d), 'Minimal strategy'). Section 505-1(g) covers assessment and modification of an approved strategy. The statute also says 'in the 7th year', not 'at 7 years'.
correct: Per 21 USC 355-1(d), a REMS must include a timetable for assessments by 18 months and 3 years after initial approval and in the 7th year after approval, unless FDA specifies otherwise.

quote: debarment certification (21 CFR 314.50(a)(5)(iv))
error: 21 CFR 314.50(a)(5) is the signature and countersignature requirement for the application form, and it has no subparagraph (iv). The NDA debarment certification comes from FD&C Act section 306(k)(1) (21 USC 335a(k)(1)), not from 314.50(a)(5)(iv).
correct: Debarment certification under FD&C Act section 306(k)(1) (21 USC 335a(k)(1)).

quote: Debarment Certification (21 CFR 314.50(a)(5)(iv)) Complete
error: Same nonexistent citation as line 2167. 314.50(a)(5) is the signature requirement and has no (iv). The debarment certification is required by FD&C Act 306(k)(1).
correct: Debarment Certification (FD&C Act section 306(k)(1); 21 USC 335a(k)(1)) Complete

quote: Form FDA 356h (Application to Market a New Drug, Biologic, or Antibiotic Drug for Human Use)
error: This is the old title of Form FDA 356h. The antibiotic category was dropped after FDAMA 1997, and the current form has a different title.
correct: Form FDA 356h, 'Application to Market a New or Abbreviated New Drug or Biologic for Human Use'.

quote: PMC 3: Renal impairment PK study (Child-Pugh classification).
error: Child-Pugh classifies hepatic impairment, not renal impairment. Renal impairment studies stratify by eGFR/CrCl (e.g., mild/moderate/severe/ESRD).
correct: PMC 3: Renal impairment PK study (stratified by eGFR/creatinine clearance); Child-Pugh applies to a hepatic impairment study.

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) and ICH E2D "Post-Approval Safety Data Management," all deaths and serious adverse events must be thoroughly analyzed.
error: ICH E2D covers post-approval safety data, so it is not the basis for analysing deaths and SAEs in a pre-approval clinical program for an NDA. 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the safety-update provision, not a deaths/SAE analysis requirement. The pre-approval framework is ICH E2A, ICH E3 section 12.3 and the ISS under 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a).
correct: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a) (integrated summary of safety), ICH E3 section 12.3 and ICH E2A, deaths and SAEs must be analysed; ICH E2D applies post-approval.

quote: reference: '21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b); ICH E2A; ICH E2D',
error: ICH E2D is a post-approval guideline and does not govern analysis of drug-related deaths in the NDA clinical program. 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the safety-update requirement.
correct: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a); ICH E2A; ICH E3 section 12.3

quote: FDA may require a REMS (with Medication Guide as a minimum element) when a boxed warning is warranted
error: A Medication Guide is not a minimum element of a REMS. Under 21 USC 355-1(d) the only required minimum is a timetable for assessments; a Medication Guide, communication plan and ETASU are each optional elements (355-1(e),(f)). A boxed warning also does not by itself trigger a REMS.
correct: FDA may require a REMS under 21 USC 355-1, which may include a Medication Guide, a communication plan and/or ETASU; the statutory minimum is a timetable for assessments.

quote: label: 'Post-Marketing Requirements (PMEs) — Mandatory Studies',
error: FDA's term for mandatory postmarketing studies under FD&C Act 505(o)(3) is 'postmarketing requirements (PMRs)'. 'PME' is not an FDA term, and the file's own placeholder uses 'PMR'.
correct: Post-Marketing Requirements (PMRs) — Mandatory Studies

quote: FDAAA Section 505(o)(3)
error: Section 505(o)(3) is a section of the FD&C Act (added by FDAAA section 901), not a section of FDAAA. The same guidance also calls PMRs 'PMEs' (line 1916).
correct: FD&C Act section 505(o)(3) (21 USC 355(o)(3)), added by FDAAA section 901.

quote: Per FDA Guidance and ICH E1/E7, sponsors should analyze PK and safety data by sex.
error: Neither guideline covers sex-based analysis. ICH E1 covers the extent of population exposure for long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, and ICH E7 covers geriatric populations.
correct: Sex-based analysis is addressed by FDA guidance (e.g., 'Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data in Medical Device Clinical Studies' for devices; for drugs, the 1993 FDA gender guideline and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(v)-(vi) requiring effectiveness and safety data by gender, age and race), not ICH E1/E7.

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1), the NDA must contain a full description of the drug substance, its mechanism of action, dosage form, route, and all proposed strengths.
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1) is the chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) technical section. It requires a description of the drug substance's physical/chemical characteristics, manufacture and controls, but not the mechanism of action or the proposed brand name. Mechanism and pharmacologic class belong to the application summary (314.50(c)) and the labeling (201.57(c)(13)).
correct: 314.50(d)(1) requires the CMC description of the drug substance and drug product; mechanism of action is presented in the summary (314.50(c)) and in labeling section 12.1 (21 CFR 201.57(c)(13)).

quote: All sequence numbers must follow the FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents (CTOCh) and CDER/CBER numbering conventions.
error: The FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy defines the CTD/eCTD heading structure, not eCTD sequence numbering. Sequence numbering is set by the FDA eCTD technical specifications / eCTD Technical Conformance Guide.
correct: Document placement must follow the FDA Comprehensive Table of Contents Headings and Hierarchy; sequence numbering follows the FDA eCTD technical specifications and eCTD Technical Conformance Guide.

quote: The standard battery includes Ames test, in vitro chromosomal aberration or micronucleus, and in vivo micronucleus assay.
error: ICH S2(R1) has two acceptable standard battery options. Option 2 is the Ames test plus an in vivo assessment in two tissues, and it has no in vitro mammalian cell test. So the in vitro chromosomal aberration or micronucleus test is not a required part of a complete S2(R1) battery.
correct: ICH S2(R1) Option 1: Ames + in vitro mammalian cell test (chromosomal aberration, micronucleus or mouse lymphoma TK) + in vivo micronucleus/chromosomal damage assay. Option 2: Ames + in vivo assessment in two tissues (e.g., micronucleus plus a second in vivo assay such as comet).

quote: Standard battery: (1) bacterial reverse mutation (Ames test), (2) in vitro chromosomal aberration or micronucleus assay, (3) in vivo micronucleus or equivalent.
error: This presents S2(R1) Option 1 as the only standard battery. ICH S2(R1) also accepts Option 2 (Ames + in vivo genotoxicity assessment in two tissues), which has no in vitro mammalian test.
correct: ICH S2(R1) allows either Option 1 (Ames + in vitro mammalian cell test + in vivo test) or Option 2 (Ames + in vivo assessment with two tissues/endpoints).

quote: FDA Guidance: In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies (2020); FDA Guidance: Clinical Drug Interaction Studies (2020)
error: Both 2020 FDA DDI guidances were withdrawn and replaced by ICH M12 (FDA final guidance, August 2024). Citing them as current is wrong.
correct: ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies (FDA final guidance, 2024); the companion Q&A may also be cited.

quote: FDA Guidance: Format and Content of Proposed REMS (2009)
error: The 2009 draft guidance 'Format and Content of Proposed Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS), REMS Assessments, and Proposed REMS Modifications' was superseded. It is cited as current.
correct: FDA guidance 'Format and Content of a REMS Document' (final, October 2017), together with the current REMS guidances.

quote: FDA Guidance: General Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Pediatric Studies (2014)
error: The December 2014 document was a draft. It was superseded by the final guidance of September 2022, which carries a different title.
correct: FDA Guidance: General Clinical Pharmacology Considerations for Pediatric Studies of Drugs, Including Biological Products (final, 2022).

quote: FDA Guidance: Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products -- Content and Format of the Pregnancy and Lactation Subsections
error: No FDA guidance has this title. The PLLR implementation guidance has a different name.
correct: FDA draft guidance 'Pregnancy, Lactation, and Reproductive Potential: Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products — Content and Format' (draft Dec 2014; revised draft July 2020).

quote: Manufacturing establishments must be registered with FDA per 21 CFR 207.20 and must have an FEI number.
error: Section 207.20 ('Who must register') belongs to the pre-2016 Part 207. The 2016 rewrite of Part 207 moved the registration obligation to 207.17. Part 207 also requires a unique facility identifier (FDA designated the DUNS number), not an FEI.
correct: Registration is required under FD&C Act 510 and 21 CFR 207.17, with registration information under 207.25, including a unique facility identifier (DUNS). An FEI is assigned by FDA, but Part 207 does not require it.

quote: FDA Guidance: Dosage and Administration Section (2018)
error: The year is wrong. The FDA guidance on the D&A section was issued as a draft in 2010 and finalized in 2023, not 2018.
correct: FDA Guidance: Dosage and Administration Section of Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products — Content and Format (final, 2023).

quote: Previously approved drugs must convert per the implementation timeline in 71 FR 3922.
error: Under 21 CFR 201.56(b) and 71 FR 3922, only applications approved from June 30, 2001 onward (plus new ones and certain efficacy supplements) must convert to PLR format. Drugs approved earlier are not required to convert; they may stay in 201.80 format.
correct: Under 201.56(b)(1), PLR conversion is required for applications approved on or after June 30, 2001 and for new submissions. Older labeling may stay in the 201.80 format unless converted voluntarily or triggered by a qualifying supplement.

quote: FDA MAPP 6020.3 (NDA Review Timelines)
error: MAPP 6020.3 is CDER's 'Review Designation Policy: Priority (P) and Standard (S)'. It is not a document on 'NDA Review Timelines'.
correct: MAPP 6020.3, Review Designation Policy: Priority (P) and Standard (S). The review clocks themselves are set by the PDUFA VII Commitment Letter.

quote: 21 CFR 314.101(d); FDA Guidance: Refuse to File (2017); MAPP 5000.3
error: CDER's refuse-to-file MAPP is MAPP 6025.4 (Good Review Practice: Refuse to File). MAPP 5000.3 is not the RTF procedure.
correct: 21 CFR 314.101; FDA Guidance: Refuse to File: NDA and BLA Submissions to CDER (2017); MAPP 6025.4.

quote: eCTD format is mandatory for all NDA submissions as of May 5, 2017 per FDA Guidance and 21 CFR 314.50(l).
error: The eCTD mandate comes from FD&C Act section 745A(a), implemented through FDA's binding eCTD guidance. 21 CFR 314.50(l) covers the format of an original application (archival copy, and content of labeling in electronic form). It does not impose eCTD.
correct: Under FD&C Act section 745A(a) and FDA guidance 'Providing Regulatory Submissions in Electronic Format — Certain Human Pharmaceutical Product Applications and Related Submissions Using the eCTD Specifications', eCTD has been required for NDAs since May 5, 2017.

quote: a bridging bioequivalence study must be provided per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1) and ICH M4Q.
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1) is the CMC technical section. Bioavailability and bioequivalence data, including bridging BE studies, belong to the human pharmacokinetics and bioavailability section, 21 CFR 314.50(d)(3) (with Part 320).
correct: Bridging BA/BE data go under 21 CFR 314.50(d)(3) and 21 CFR Part 320, filed in CTD Module 5.3.1 and summarized in 2.7.1.

quote: FDA Guidance: Indication-Specific Labeling (2018)
error: No FDA guidance is titled 'Indication-Specific Labeling'. The 2018 document on this topic is a draft on the Indications and Usage section.
correct: FDA draft guidance 'Indications and Usage Section of Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products — Content and Format' (2018).

quote: FDA Guidance: Drug Shortage Management (2020)
error: No FDA guidance is titled 'Drug Shortage Management'. The 2020 final guidance implementing section 506C has a different title.
correct: FDA Guidance: Notifying FDA of a Permanent Discontinuance or Interruption in Manufacturing Under Section 506C of the FD&C Act (final, 2020).

quote: FDA Guidance: Pre-Approval Inspections (2020)
error: Pre-approval inspections are governed by FDA Compliance Program 7346.832 (Preapproval Inspections). That is a compliance program, not a 2020 guidance.
correct: FDA Compliance Program Guidance Manual 7346.832, Preapproval Inspections.

quote: Provide process validation data at commercial scale, including at least three consecutive production batches demonstrating process consistency
error: This recommendation cites FDA's 2011 Process Validation guidance for a three-consecutive-batch requirement. That guidance dropped the fixed 'three batches' expectation: the number of PPQ batches is set by the manufacturer from risk and process knowledge. The guidance also does not require PPQ data in the NDA. PPQ must be finished before commercial distribution, not before approval. Line 583 says the CMC section 'must demonstrate that the manufacturing process is validated at commercial scale per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1)'. That is also not an NDA requirement; for most non-sterile processes, PPQ data are not submitted in the application.
correct: Under the 2011 Process Validation guidance, the number of PPQ batches is justified by the manufacturer (no fixed three-batch minimum). PPQ must be completed and the process qualified before commercial distribution. The NDA describes the commercial process and controls. It does not have to contain commercial-scale validation data, except for items such as sterilization validation.

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(9), the Use in Specific Populations section must address dosing in hepatic and renal impairment
error: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(9) requires subsections on pregnancy, lactation, females and males of reproductive potential, pediatric use and geriatric use. Renal and hepatic impairment are optional additional subsections, included when data on those subpopulations are available. The regulation does not require them.
correct: Under 21 CFR 201.57(c)(9), additional subsections such as renal or hepatic impairment may be included when sufficient data are available. They are expected when relevant but are not a required subsection.

quote: The eCTD backbone itself provides structural navigation, but a reader-friendly ToC document is also expected.
error: For an eCTD submission, the XML backbone serves as the comprehensive table of contents that 21 CFR 314.50(b) requires. FDA's eCTD specifications say not to submit separate table-of-contents documents. A ToC document is not expected, so a missing one is not a deficiency.
correct: In eCTD, the backbone and its hierarchy satisfy the comprehensive index/ToC requirement. Separate ToC documents are not needed and should not be added to Modules 2-5.

quote: Reformat the entire submission in eCTD v4.0 format
error: This implies eCTD v4.0 is required. FDA requires eCTD format under FD&C Act 745A(a) but has not made v4.0 mandatory. Since September 2024, v4.0 has been accepted for new applications alongside eCTD v3.2.2, which is still accepted. A compliant non-eCTD submission needs eCTD, not v4.0 specifically.
correct: Reformat the submission into an FDA-supported eCTD version (v3.2.2 or v4.0). v4.0 is optional and not mandated.

quote: described in FDA's 2023 draft guidance on benefit-risk assessment
error: FDA's guidance 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products' was issued in draft in September 2021 and finalized in October 2023. The 2023 version is final guidance, not a draft. The sentence that follows ('The draft guidance is non-binding') repeats the wrong status.
correct: FDA's final guidance 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products' (October 2023; draft September 2021). Like all guidance it is non-binding.

quote: 21 CFR 801.4; FDA Guidance: Medical Device Home-Use Initiative (2023)
error: No FDA guidance has this title, and there is none from 2023. The Medical Device Home Use Initiative was a 2010 CDRH initiative, not a guidance. FDA's guidance on home-use device labeling and design is 'Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use' (final, November 2014). 21 CFR 801.4 defines 'intended uses'. It says nothing about home-use labeling.
correct: FDA Guidance: Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use (November 2014). General device labeling requirements are in 21 CFR Part 801, for example 801.5 (adequate directions for use).

quote: FDA Guidance: REMS Integration with Labeling
error: FDA has never issued a guidance titled 'REMS Integration with Labeling'. The citation names a document that does not exist.
correct: Cite real REMS guidance, for example 'REMS: FDA's Application of Statutory Factors in Determining When a REMS Is Necessary' (2019) or 'Format and Content of a REMS Document' (2017), together with 21 CFR 201.57(c)(1) for the boxed warning.

quote: FDA Guidance: Medication Guides — Distribution Requirements and Inclusion in REMS (2011)
error: This 2011 guidance covers when Medication Guides must be distributed and how they fit into REMS. It does not set or recommend a 6th-8th grade reading level, so it does not support the finding it is attached to.
correct: The readability requirement for Medication Guides is in 21 CFR 208.20(a) (nontechnical, understandable language). FDA's written consumer medication information guidance ('Useful Written Consumer Medication Information (CMI)', 2006) addresses readability.

quote: Per 21 CFR 830, all medical devices must bear a Unique Device Identifier (UDI) on their label.
error: The requirement that a device label bear a UDI is in 21 CFR 801.20, not Part 830. Part 830 sets up the UDI system: issuing agencies, UDI format and GUDID. 'All medical devices' is also wrong, because 21 CFR 801.30 lists general exceptions. The helpText at line 1265 in the same node states both points correctly.
correct: Per 21 CFR 801.20, device labels must bear a UDI, subject to the exceptions in 21 CFR 801.30. 21 CFR Part 830 governs the UDI system and GUDID data submission.

quote: Not all sections are required for every product — include only those relevant. Sections 9 (Drug Abuse and Dependence) and 16 (How Supplied / Storage and Handling) are commonly included.
error: Under 21 CFR 201.56(d), most FPI sections are mandatory. Only a few listed sections may be left out when they clearly do not apply, such as Boxed Warning, Drug Abuse and Dependence, Clinical Studies and References. Section 16 (How Supplied/Storage and Handling, 201.57(c)(17)) is required for every product, not just 'commonly included'. Contraindications (Section 4) must appear even when there are none, and then it says 'None'.
correct: FPI sections 1–8, 11–13, 16 and 17 are required. Section 4 must state 'None' if there are no contraindications. Only the sections that 201.56(d) allows to be left out when inapplicable (e.g., Boxed Warning, Section 9, 14, 15) may be dropped.

quote: list sections with substantive labeling changes within the past year
error: 21 CFR 201.57(a)(5) allows Recent Major Changes to list only five FPI sections: Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, and Warnings and Precautions. It does not cover any section with a substantive change.
correct: Recent Major Changes lists substantive changes approved or authorized within the past year, but only in the Boxed Warning, Indications and Usage, Dosage and Administration, Contraindications, or Warnings and Precautions sections, with the section number and the month/year of the change.

quote: Electronic SPL submission to FDA DailyMed is required.
error: SPL is submitted to FDA, through the Electronic Submissions Gateway as part of the application or listing. DailyMed is the National Library of Medicine's public site, which shows SPL that FDA has received. Sponsors do not submit to DailyMed. Line 204 says the same wrong thing ('submitted ... to the FDA's DailyMed system').
correct: Content of labeling is submitted to FDA in SPL format (21 CFR 314.50(l)(1)(i); 601.14). NLM's DailyMed then publishes it.

quote: All prescription drug and biologic labeling must follow the Physician Labeling Rule (PLR) format
error: PLR format is required only for applications submitted on or after June 30, 2006, and for those approved from June 30, 2001 onward, on the phased schedule. Older prescription products may keep the non-PLR format under 21 CFR 201.80 unless they convert.
correct: PLR format (21 CFR 201.56(d), 201.57) is required for new NDAs/BLAs/efficacy supplements submitted on or after June 30, 2006, and for products approved since June 30, 2001 on the implementation schedule. Older labeling may follow 21 CFR 201.80.

quote: Inactive ingredients, and Questions? phone number.
error: Under 21 CFR 201.66(c)(9), the 'Questions?' / 'Questions or comments?' heading with a phone number is optional in Drug Facts, not a required element.
correct: The 'Questions?' heading and phone number may be included in Drug Facts (optional per 201.66(c)(9)). Separately, a domestic address or phone number for adverse event reporting is required on the label under FD&C Act 502(x).

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance: Medication Guides — Distribution Requirements and Inclusion in REMS (2011)'
error: The cited guidance covers when and how Medication Guides are distributed, and when they fall within REMS. It does not set a 6th–8th grade reading level. 21 CFR 208.20 requires only nontechnical, understandable language and does not name a grade level.
correct: 21 CFR 208.20 requires Medication Guides to be written in nontechnical, understandable language. A 6th–8th grade target is a health-literacy best practice, not something this guidance recommends.

quote: FDA Guidance: Medical Device Home-Use Initiative (2023)
error: No FDA guidance has this title or date. The Medical Device Home Use Initiative was launched in 2010. The guidance on home-use device labeling and design is 'Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use', final November 2014. 21 CFR 801.4 defines intended use and does not set home-use labeling requirements.
correct: FDA Guidance: Design Considerations for Devices Intended for Home Use (November 2014). Home-use labeling recommendations come from guidance, not from 21 CFR 801.4.

quote: FDA Advisory Committee briefing documents must present a complete summary of efficacy findings from all adequate and well-controlled studies per 21 CFR 314.126.
error: 21 CFR 314.126 defines what makes a study adequate and well-controlled for substantial evidence. It does not set any content requirement for advisory committee briefing documents.
correct: 21 CFR 314.126 sets the characteristics of adequate and well-controlled investigations. Briefing-document content is guided by FDA's advisory committee guidance, and 314.126 does not mandate it.

quote: Per 21 CFR 610.2, samples and protocols must be submitted to CBER for lot release before distribution of vaccines and blood products.
error: 21 CFR 610.2(a) does not impose automatic lot release on every vaccine and blood product. CBER can require samples and protocols for any lot at any time, and a lot may not be distributed before release only after the manufacturer is notified by the Director, CBER. Whole blood and blood components are also generally not subject to CBER lot release. Plasma derivatives can be, when CBER so notifies the manufacturer.
correct: Under 21 CFR 610.2(a), CBER may require samples of any lot, with protocols, at any time. Once the manufacturer has been notified by the Director, CBER, it may not distribute a lot until CBER releases it. Most vaccines and plasma-derived products are under routine lot release by such notification. It is not a blanket requirement for all blood products.

quote: Fewer lots may not provide sufficient statistical power for the tiered analytical similarity assessment.
error: This text points to the tiered (Tier 1/2/3) analytical similarity approach. FDA withdrew that approach in 2018, as this file's own guidance at line 2033 says. The current 2019 draft comparative analytical assessment guidance uses risk-ranked quantitative or qualitative evaluation (for example, equivalence testing or a quality range), not tiers.
correct: Fewer than about 10 reference product lots may not adequately characterize reference product variability for the risk-based comparative analytical assessment, whether quantitative (for example, equivalence testing or a quality range) or qualitative. This is the approach of FDA's 2019 draft guidance on comparative analytical assessment for therapeutic protein biosimilars.

quote: { value: 'pader', label: 'PADER (Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report)' },
error: For a licensed biologic, the US periodic safety report required by 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2) is the Periodic Adverse Experience Report (PAER). The PADER is the NDA/ANDA report under 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2). The options also leave out the PBRER, which FDA accepts in place of the PAER under a waiver, as line 1845 of this file says.
correct: For a BLA, the periodic report is the PAER under 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2), or an ICH E2C(R2) PBRER submitted under an FDA waiver. PADER is the drug (21 CFR 314.80) term.

quote: Per ICH S6(R1) and ICH S8, immunotoxicity assessment is especially important for immunomodulatory biologics.
error: ICH S8 (Immunotoxicity Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals) excludes biotechnology-derived products from its scope. Its scope section says it does not apply to products covered by ICH S6. Citing S8 as authority for immunotoxicity assessment of biologics is a misapplied citation.
correct: For biologics, immunotoxicity assessment is covered by ICH S6(R1) (Part I section 4.5, and the immunomodulation considerations in the Addendum). ICH S8 applies to small-molecule pharmaceuticals and explicitly excludes biotechnology-derived products.

quote: Per 42 USC 262(c) and 21 CFR 600.21, FDA must inspect and approve the manufacturing facility before a BLA can be licensed.
error: 42 USC 262(c) is FDA's general authority to inspect biologics establishments, and 21 CFR 600.21 covers when inspections take place. Neither one sets the rule that a license issues only after inspection. That rule is in 21 CFR 601.20(d). The same pairing is cited again at line 816, and line 817 gives '21 CFR 600.21' as the reference.
correct: The pre-license inspection requirement is 21 CFR 601.20(d): a biologics license is issued only after inspection of the establishment(s) listed in the application. 21 CFR 600.21 covers inspection timing, and 42 USC 262(c) gives the inspection authority.

quote: should be included in Module 3.2.S.7.1 (DS) or 3.2.P.8.1 (DP) of the CTD
error: In ICH M4Q, 3.2.S.7.1 and 3.2.P.8.1 are 'Stability Summary and Conclusions'. The stability protocol does not go there.
correct: The post-approval stability protocol and stability commitment go in 3.2.S.7.2 (DS) and 3.2.P.8.2 (DP). Stability data go in 3.2.S.7.3 and 3.2.P.8.3. The same wrong section numbers appear in the reference string on line 691.

quote: including identification and qualification of all impurities above reporting thresholds
error: ICH Q3A(R2) does not require every impurity above the reporting threshold to be identified and qualified. It sets three separate thresholds: reporting, identification and qualification.
correct: Impurities above the reporting threshold are reported. Those above the identification threshold are structurally identified. Those above the qualification threshold are qualified. The thresholds are in Q3A(R2)/Q3B(R2) Attachment 1.

quote: ICH Q1E permits shelf life extrapolation beyond observed data only when statistical analysis supports the projection and no significant change is observed.
error: This misstates ICH Q1E. Extrapolation does not always need statistical support. When data show little or no change over time and little or no variability, Q1E says statistical analysis is normally unnecessary and still allows extrapolation. Extrapolation is also possible, with limits, when there is significant change at the intermediate condition but not at the accelerated condition.
correct: Under ICH Q1E, the allowed extrapolation depends on the data. With no significant change at accelerated and little variability, the shelf life can be up to twice the long-term data period, but no more than 12 months beyond it, and statistical analysis is normally unnecessary. In other cases statistical analysis supports a smaller extrapolation (for example, 1.5x, but no more than 6 months beyond the data).

quote: (e.g., pure red cell aplasia with EPO, acquired hemophilia with Factor VIII)
error: Acquired hemophilia is a spontaneous autoimmune disease. It is not caused by ADA from a therapeutic protein cross-reacting with an endogenous counterpart. FVIII inhibitors in hemophilia A patients act against a replacement protein the patient lacks, so they are not an example of neutralizing an endogenous protein.
correct: The standard examples of cross-reactive neutralization of an endogenous protein, including in FDA's 2014 immunogenicity guidance, are pure red cell aplasia with recombinant erythropoietin and thrombocytopenia with PEG-rHuMGDF (megakaryocyte growth and development factor).

error: 9 CFR Part 113 is USDA's standard requirements for veterinary biologics under the Virus-Serum-Toxin Act. It does not apply to a human BLA. The same wrong citation appears on line 811.
correct: For human biologics, viral safety rests on ICH Q5A(R2), 21 CFR 610 (for example, 610.18 on cultures) and FDA guidance. 9 CFR 113 should not be cited for a BLA.

quote: Per 42 USC 262(c), FDA must inspect and approve the establishment before a biologics license can be issued.
error: 42 USC 262(c) only authorizes inspection of establishments. It does not require a pre-license inspection and approval.
correct: The pre-license inspection requirement is 21 CFR 601.20(d): a license is issued only after the establishment has been inspected and found to comply. Licensure also depends on the facility meeting standards under 42 USC 262(a)(2)(C). The same citation is used on line 389.

quote: 'ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.3; FDA Guidance: Quality Considerations for Continuous Manufacturing (2019)'
error: ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.3 covers manufacturing process development, not drug-excipient compatibility. The continuous manufacturing guidance does not address excipient compatibility either.
correct: ICH Q8(R2) covers drug substance-excipient compatibility in Section 2.1.1 (Drug Substance), under 2.1 Components of the Drug Product.

quote: 'ICH Q3A(R2) Table 1; ICH Q3B(R2) Table 1;
error: ICH Q3A(R2) and Q3B(R2) put their reporting, identification and qualification thresholds in Attachment 1. Neither guideline has a 'Table 1'.
correct: ICH Q3A(R2) Attachment 1 (Thresholds); ICH Q3B(R2) Attachment 1 (Thresholds for Degradation Products in New Drug Products).

quote: FDA requires nitrosamine risk evaluations per the September 2020 guidance
error: The text cites the September 2020 original (and the February 2021 Rev. 1 on line 788) as if it were current. FDA issued Revision 2 of 'Control of Nitrosamine Impurities in Human Drugs' in September 2024. Rev. 2 is the version in force, and it adds the NDSRI recommended acceptable-intake framework.
correct: FDA Guidance: Control of Nitrosamine Impurities in Human Drugs, Revision 2 (September 2024).

quote: FDA Guidance on Comparability Protocols (2016)
error: The 2016 document was a draft guidance ('Comparability Protocols for Human Drugs and Biologics: CMC Information', April 2016). FDA replaced it with a final guidance in October 2022, so citing the 2016 draft as current is wrong.
correct: FDA Guidance: Comparability Protocols for Postapproval Changes to the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Information in an NDA, ANDA, or BLA (final, October 2022).

quote: 'ICH Q1E; ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.5; FDA Guidance: Stability Testing (2014)'
error: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.5 is 'Specification'. Evaluating stability data and extrapolating shelf life is covered in Section 2.2.9 (Evaluation), together with Q1E.
correct: ICH Q1E; ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.9 (Evaluation), or 2.1.9 for drug substance.

quote: required per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1)(ii)(b)
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1)(ii)(b) requires the proposed or actual master production record. The drug product description, including components, packaging and controls, is under (d)(1)(ii)(a). The same citation is repeated on line 126.
correct: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1)(ii)(a) for the drug product description. The container closure system description is filed in CTD 3.2.P.7.

quote: FDA Guidance: Genotoxic and Carcinogenic Impurities in Drug Substances and Products (2008)
error: This 2008 FDA document was only ever a draft ('Recommended Approaches'), and FDA later withdrew it in favour of ICH M7. It is not current guidance.
correct: Cite ICH M7(R2) (FDA guidance 'M7(R2) Assessment and Control of DNA Reactive (Mutagenic) Impurities in Pharmaceuticals to Limit Potential Carcinogenic Risk') only.

quote: WHO TRS 961 Annex 7 recommend a structured technology transfer process
error: WHO TRS 961 Annex 7 (2011) has been replaced by the revised WHO guidelines on technology transfer in pharmaceutical manufacturing, published as WHO TRS 1044 Annex 4 (2022). The same citation is repeated on line 597.
correct: WHO TRS 1044 (2022), Annex 4: WHO guidelines on technology transfer in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

quote: ICH Q6A Decision Tree #6
error: ICH Q6A Decision Tree #6 covers microbiological quality attributes of drug substances and excipients. This finding is about drug product microbiological controls by route of administration. In Q6A, Decision Tree #8 covers non-sterile drug products, and no decision tree covers sterile products.
correct: ICH Q6A Decision Tree #8 (Microbiological Attributes of Non-sterile Drug Products). For sterile products, cite 21 CFR 211.113(b) and USP <71>/<85>.

quote: FDA Guidance: Setting Specifications for Biotechnological/Biological Products (1999)
error: No FDA guidance has this title. The 1999 FDA document is the published version of ICH Q6B itself.
correct: FDA Guidance for Industry: Q6B Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for Biotechnological/Biological Products (August 1999).

quote: FDA Guidance: Elemental Impurities in Drug Products (2022)
error: FDA's final guidance 'Elemental Impurities in Drug Products' was issued in August 2018. The 2022 FDA document is the ICH Q3D(R2) guideline, not this guidance.
correct: FDA Guidance: Elemental Impurities in Drug Products (August 2018); ICH Q3D(R2) (2022).

quote: ICH Q6A Section 3.1 and S.3.1 of the CTD require comprehensive structural elucidation
error: ICH Q6A Section 3.1 is 'Specifications: Definition and Justification' (the same file cites it that way on line 246). It does not set structural elucidation requirements. Structural elucidation belongs in CTD 3.2.S.3.1 under ICH M4Q.
correct: ICH M4Q(R1) 3.2.S.3.1 (Elucidation of Structure and other Characteristics). Q6A Section 3.1 is not the source.

quote: reference: 'ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6',
error: ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6 does not cover risk assessment. In Part I, Section 2.6 is 'Compatibility'. In Part II (the Annex), Section 2.6 is 'Product Lifecycle Management and Continual Improvement'.
correct: The section on risk assessment for identifying CPPs and CQAs is ICH Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.3, 'Risk Assessment: Linking Material Attributes and Process Parameters to Drug Product CQAs'.

quote: 'Per ICH Q6A (Section 3.1) for small molecules and Q6B (Section 3) for biologics, provide evidence confirming the molecular structure.
error: ICH Q6A Section 3.1 is 'Specifications: Definition and Justification', and ICH Q6B Section 3 is 'Justification of the Specification'. Neither section covers structural characterization.
correct: Characterization of biotech products is in ICH Q6B Section 2.1 ('Characterisation', which includes physicochemical properties and structure). Structure elucidation evidence goes in CTD 3.2.S.3.1 (ICH M4Q). Q6A does not have a structural-characterization section.

quote: 'Per ICH Q6A (Section 3) and Q6B (Section 3), characterize relevant physicochemical properties
error: ICH Q6B Section 3 is 'Justification of the Specification', not the characterization of physicochemical or higher-order structure properties.
correct: Physicochemical properties of biotech products are in ICH Q6B Section 2.1.1 ('Physicochemical properties'), under 2.1 Characterisation.

quote: reference: 'ICH Q11, FDA Guidance on Drug Shortages (2023)',
error: I know of no FDA guidance titled 'Drug Shortages' issued in 2023. The citation looks invented.
correct: Cite a real FDA guidance. 'Risk Management Plans to Mitigate the Potential for Drug Shortages' was a draft in May 2022. 'Notifying FDA of a Permanent Discontinuance or Interruption in Manufacturing Under Section 506C of the FD&C Act' covers shortage notification.

quote: 'Per ICH Q1A(R2)–Q1F, stability studies must be conducted under defined storage conditions
error: The range Q1A(R2)–Q1F includes ICH Q1F, which ICH withdrew in 2006. It is presented here as part of the current stability guidance.
correct: Cite the stability guidances still in force (ICH Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1C, Q1D, Q1E) and note that Q1F was withdrawn in 2006. Zone III/IV conditions are now set by WHO and regional guidance.

quote: Identification threshold ≥ 0.10% or ≥ 0.05%. Qualification threshold ≥ 0.15% or ≥ 0.05%.
error: For a maximum daily dose of 2 g/day or less, ICH Q3A(R2) Attachment 1 sets the identification threshold at 0.10% or 1.0 mg per day total daily intake, whichever is lower, and the qualification threshold at 0.15% or 1.0 mg per day TDI, whichever is lower. The text leaves out the 1.0 mg/day alternative. For doses above about 0.67 g/day (qualification) or 1 g/day (identification), that alternative is the threshold that applies, so the percentages given are wrong for those doses.
correct: Q3A(R2), dose ≤2 g/day: reporting 0.05%; identification 0.10% or 1.0 mg/day TDI, whichever is lower; qualification 0.15% or 1.0 mg/day TDI, whichever is lower. Dose >2 g/day: reporting 0.03%, identification 0.05%, qualification 0.05%.

quote: Commercial processes must be validated before NDA/BLA approval.
error: FDA's 2011 Process Validation guidance ties successful PPQ to commercial distribution, not to application approval: a manufacturer must complete PPQ before any batch is commercially distributed. For NDAs there is no rule that PPQ is finished before approval. The same claim appears at line 1172 ('FDA expects PPQ to be complete before NDA/BLA approval') and line 1182. Line 1182 also contradicts itself, since it goes on to describe a commitment to complete PPQ before commercial distribution.
correct: Per FDA's Process Validation guidance (2011), PPQ must be completed successfully before commercial distribution of product. For BLAs, FDA typically expects PPQ or validation data in the application. For NDAs, PPQ can be completed after approval, as long as it is done before commercial distribution.

quote: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management, ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.6
error: Section 2.6 of ICH Q8(R2) Part I is 'Compatibility'. In the Annex (Part II), Section 2.6 is product lifecycle management. Neither covers quality risk assessment for identifying CPPs and CQAs. That topic is Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.3, 'Risk Assessment: Linking Material Attributes and Process Parameters to Drug Product CQAs'.
correct: ICH Q9, ICH Q8(R2) Part II (Annex) Section 2.3 (Risk Assessment)

quote: Per ICH Q11, starting materials should be commercially available substances with well-defined specifications.
error: ICH Q11 does not require starting materials to be commercially available. Its Section 5 criteria are that the material has defined chemical properties and structure, is not a non-isolated intermediate, is incorporated as a significant structural fragment, and sits enough steps upstream. Commercial availability is only one case discussed in the Q11 Q&A, for justifying a commercially available chemical as a starting material. It is not a general requirement.
correct: Per ICH Q11 Section 5, a starting material should be a substance with defined chemical properties and structure, controlled by an appropriate specification, and incorporated as a significant structural fragment. Commercial availability is not required.

quote: Confirmed mutagenic impurities (Class 1, 2, or 3)
error: In ICH M7, Class 3 means an alerting structure, unrelated to the drug substance structure, with no mutagenicity data. A Class 3 impurity is not a confirmed mutagen. Only Class 1 (known mutagenic carcinogens) and Class 2 (known mutagens with unknown carcinogenic potential) are confirmed mutagenic.
correct: Confirmed mutagenic impurities are ICH M7 Class 1 or 2. Class 3 impurities have alerts but no data, and are treated as mutagenic until tested, for example by an Ames test.

quote: Per ICH Q1A(R2)–Q1F, stability studies must be conducted
error: ICH Q1F (Stability Data Package for Registration Applications in Climatic Zones III and IV) was withdrawn by ICH in 2006. It is not a guideline in force and should not be cited as part of the current stability guidance set. The file header comment repeats the citation, but that comment is not shown to clients.
correct: Cite ICH Q1A(R2) through Q1E (Q1A(R2), Q1B, Q1C, Q1D, Q1E). For Zone III/IV conditions, refer to WHO stability guidance (TRS 1010 Annex 10). Q1F was withdrawn in 2006.

quote: 30°C / 65% RH (Long-Term, Zone III/IV)
error: 30°C/65% RH as the long-term condition for Zones III and IV came from ICH Q1F, which was withdrawn in 2006. Under current WHO zone definitions, 30°C/65% RH is Zone IVa only. Zone III is 30°C/35% RH and Zone IVb is 30°C/75% RH. The same label appears at line 164 for the drug product.
correct: 30°C/65% RH is the long-term condition for Zone IVa, and an ICH Q1A(R2) alternative long-term condition. Zone IVb is 30°C/75% RH and Zone III is 30°C/35% RH.

quote: 'ICH Q1A(R2); 21 CFR 211.166; FDA Guidance for Industry: Stability Testing (2004)'
error: FDA never issued a 2004 guidance titled 'Stability Testing'. The FDA document with that name was the June 1998 draft 'Stability Testing of Drug Substances and Drug Products'. It was never finalised and was later withdrawn in favour of ICH Q1A(R2) (FDA adoption Nov 2003) and Q1E (FDA adoption June 2004). The same nonexistent citation appears again at lines 329, 460, 634, 657, 736 and 760, and in the module header.
correct: Cite ICH Q1A(R2) (FDA guidance, Nov 2003) and/or ICH Q1E 'Evaluation of Stability Data' (FDA guidance, June 2004). Do not cite an 'FDA Guidance for Industry: Stability Testing (2004)'.

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance for Industry: Stability Testing; EMA Note for Guidance on In-Use Stability Testing
error: No current FDA guidance called 'Stability Testing' exists. The 1998 draft of that name was never finalised and was withdrawn. FDA also has no stability guidance that sets in-use stability expectations.
correct: Cite EMA CPMP/QWP/2934/99 (correct as given) and, for the US, ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.1 (testing after constitution/dilution) or 21 CFR 211.166(a)(5). Remove the nonexistent FDA title.

quote: WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 defines long-term storage conditions by climatic zone
error: WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 (2009) is superseded. WHO replaced it in 2018 with TRS 1010, Annex 10, 'Stability testing of active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished pharmaceutical products', which also updated the country zone list. The superseded document is cited as current here and at lines 344, 360, 474 and 493, and in auditor lines 360-361.
correct: WHO TRS 1010 (2018), Annex 10 (which replaced TRS 953 Annex 2) defines the climatic zones and long-term conditions, including Zone IVb at 30 C/75% RH. WHO Prequalification applies this guideline.

quote: 'ICH Q1F (withdrawn but referenced by WHO) and WHO Technical Report Series No. 953 require long-term stability testing at 30 ± 2 °C / 35 ± 5% RH (Zone III)
error: The finding says ICH Q1F requires these zone conditions. Q1F was withdrawn in 2006 and requires nothing. It also never specified 30 C/35% RH for Zone III or 30 C/75% RH for Zone IVb: it set one 30 C/65% RH long-term condition for Zones III and IV, and it had no Zone IVb. The reference on line 361 and the question on line 341 ('ICH Q1F and WHO guidelines require') also present Q1F as a current requirement.
correct: The zone-specific long-term conditions (Zone III 30/35, IVa 30/65, IVb 30/75) come from the WHO stability guideline, now TRS 1010 Annex 10 (2018). ICH Q1F was withdrawn in 2006 and should not be cited as a requirement.

quote: ICH Q1F was withdrawn from the ICH process in 2006 but remains adopted by WHO and several national regulatory authorities.
error: WHO did not adopt ICH Q1F. After Q1F was withdrawn, ICH left the zone conditions to WHO, which issued its own guideline (TRS 953 Annex 2, now TRS 1010 Annex 10) with different conditions, including Zone IVb. The question on line 472 also says Q1F 'provides guidance for registration in Climatic Zones III and IV' as if it were in force.
correct: ICH Q1F was withdrawn in 2006. Zone III/IV conditions are now set by the WHO stability guideline (TRS 1010 Annex 10, which superseded TRS 953 Annex 2) and by regional authorities (e.g., ASEAN, 30 C/75% RH).

quote: per FDA Guidance for Industry "Container Closure System Guidance for Human Drug Products."
error: The FDA guidance title is wrong. The 1999 guidance is 'Container Closure Systems for Packaging Human Drugs and Biologics'. The low-humidity testing for semi-permeable containers also comes from ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.3, not from that FDA guidance.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.3 (drug products in semi-permeable containers) sets the low-RH testing. Its companion is FDA Guidance for Industry 'Container Closure Systems for Packaging Human Drugs and Biologics' (May 1999).

quote: and the shelf life should be based on long-term data without extrapolation.
