error: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.1 only says that significant change at accelerated triggers intermediate testing. It does not forbid extrapolation. ICH Q1E (Appendix A, Section 2.4) allows limited extrapolation, up to 1.5x and no more than 6 months beyond the long-term data, when significant change occurs at accelerated but not at intermediate. The recommendation on line 711 ('Limit shelf life to available long-term data without extrapolation') repeats the error.
correct: Under ICH Q1A(R2) 2.2.7.1, significant change at accelerated triggers intermediate testing. Under ICH Q1E Section 2.4.1.2 and Appendix A, if the intermediate data show no significant change, limited extrapolation (up to 1.5x, not more than 6 months beyond the long-term data) may be justified. No extrapolation is allowed only when significant change also occurs at intermediate.

quote: 21 CFR 211.150 requires appropriate storage during distribution
error: 21 CFR 211.150 (Distribution procedures) requires only FIFO stock rotation (a) and a lot-distribution system that allows recall (b). It contains no requirement for storage conditions during distribution. Storage under appropriate conditions is in 21 CFR 211.142 (Warehousing procedures).
correct: 21 CFR 211.142(b) requires storage under appropriate conditions of temperature, humidity and light. 21 CFR 211.150 covers distribution procedures (FIFO and recall traceability).

quote: FDA Guidance: Content and Format of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls Information for a Therapeutic Recombinant DNA-Derived Product (1996)
error: The 1996 FDA/CBER guidance title is misstated.
correct: 'Guidance for Industry for the Submission of Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls Information for a Therapeutic Recombinant DNA-Derived Product or a Monoclonal Antibody Product for In Vivo Use' (August 1996).

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.8 expects the post-approval stability protocol to be described in CTD Module 3.2.P.8.2 (drug product) or 3.2.S.7.2 (drug substance).
error: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.8 (Stability Commitment) does not mention CTD section numbers. The 3.2.P.8.2 / 3.2.S.7.2 placement of the post-approval stability protocol and commitment is set by ICH M4Q (CTD Quality).
correct: ICH M4Q places the post-approval stability protocol and stability commitment in 3.2.S.7.2 (drug substance) and 3.2.P.8.2 (drug product). ICH Q1A(R2) 2.1.8/2.2.8 describe the commitment itself.

quote: a field alert report must be submitted within 3 working days of a confirmed stability failure on a distributed batch.
error: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1) requires the field alert within three working days of the applicant's receipt of the information. It is not conditioned on the failure being confirmed. FDA's Field Alert Report guidance (2021) says to file the initial FAR within 3 working days even if the investigation is not complete.
correct: Per 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1), submit a field alert report within three working days of receiving information about a distributed batch's failure to meet specification (or a significant change or deterioration), with follow-up reports as the investigation proceeds. Confirmation is not a prerequisite.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1 further distinguishes requirements for drug substances versus drug products.
error: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1 covers only the drug substance. The drug product is Section 2.2, and it is Section 2 (Guidelines) that sets the two apart.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1 (Drug Substance) and Section 2.2 (Drug Product) set out the separate requirements.

quote: description: 'Brazil, Ghana, Philippines'
error: These three countries are given as examples of Zone IVa (30 C / 65% RH). They are Zone IVb markets. WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 lists Brazil, Ghana and the Philippines as IVb. ANVISA requires 30 C / 75% RH, and ASEAN, which includes the Philippines, adopted 30 C / 75% RH. A sponsor who follows this label could plan 30/65 long-term data for markets that require 30/75.
correct: Brazil, Ghana and the Philippines are Zone IVb (hot/very humid, 30 C / 75% RH long-term). They should not be listed as Zone IVa examples.

quote: The proposed shelf life should not exceed the available long-term data by more than 2x (e.g., 12 months data allows a maximum 24-month shelf-life claim).
error: This states 2x as the limit and leaves out the other half of the ICH Q1E rule: no more than 12 months beyond the long-term data. It also leaves out the narrower limits that apply when there is significant change at accelerated, for refrigerated products (1.5x, at most +6 months), and for frozen products (no extrapolation). For example, 24 months of data does not allow a 48-month claim, only 36. The same 2x-only rule appears at line 905, line 991 and line 1046 ('generally no more than twice').
correct: ICH Q1E Appendix A / 2.4.1.2: for room-temperature products with no significant change at accelerated, extrapolation may be up to twice the long-term data, but no more than 12 months beyond it. Refrigerated products: up to 1.5x, at most +6 months. Frozen products: no extrapolation.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7 requires six months of accelerated stability data (40 C/75% RH) at the time of submission.
error: This presents 40 C / 75% RH accelerated data as a universal requirement. Under Q1A(R2) 2.2.7, 40/75 is the accelerated condition only for the general (room-temperature) case. For refrigerated products the accelerated condition is 25 C / 60% RH. For freezer products there is no standard accelerated study (a single batch is tested at an elevated temperature). The check fires on any 'No', including refrigerated and frozen products, and calls the absence of 40/75 data a likely Refuse-to-File. Line 383 makes the same unconditional claim.
correct: Six months of accelerated data is expected at submission for room-temperature products (40 C / 75% RH). For refrigerated products the accelerated condition is 25 C / 60% RH (Q1A(R2) 2.2.7.3). For freezer storage, an elevated-temperature study on a single batch applies instead (2.2.7.5).

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.8 states that a post-approval stability protocol and commitment should be provided in the registration application. The commitment typically includes placing at least one production batch per year
error: This misstates Q1A(R2) 2.2.8. The stability commitment there applies only when the long-term data on production batches do not cover the proposed shelf life. It requires either continuing the studies through the shelf life or placing more production batches on study to total at least three. The annual 'one production batch per year' program comes from FDA/cGMP practice (21 CFR 211.166). Q1A(R2) 2.2.8 does not contain it.
correct: Q1A(R2) 2.2.8: when the available long-term data on production batches do not cover the proposed shelf life, commit to continue the studies through the shelf life, or to place more production batches on study until there are at least three, using the same protocol as the primary batches. The annual-batch program is a separate FDA/cGMP expectation.

quote: additional studies at low humidity may be needed per FDA Guidance for Industry "Container Closure System Guidance for Human Drug Products."
error: The low-relative-humidity stability requirement for aqueous products in semi-permeable containers comes from ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.4 (Drug products packaged in semi-permeable containers). The FDA container closure guidance (1999) does not set out this storage-condition study.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) 2.2.7.4 requires aqueous products in semi-permeable containers to be evaluated for water loss under low-RH conditions (for example, 25 C / 40% RH long-term, or 40 C / not more than 25% RH accelerated).

quote: FDA conducts a pre-approval inspection for most PMA applications per 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4)
error: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4) sets out what the PMA application must contain: a complete description of the device, its components, properties and principles of operation, and the methods, facilities and controls used to manufacture it. It says nothing about FDA conducting a pre-approval inspection, so it is the wrong citation for that statement.
correct: Pre-approval inspection is FDA's practice in the PMA review under 21 CFR 814.44 (approval may depend on a finding that the manufacturing facilities, methods and controls comply with 21 CFR Part 820). Under 21 CFR 814.45(a)(3), FDA may deny approval if the facilities, methods or controls do not conform to Part 820. 814.20(b)(4) is only the application-content requirement for the manufacturing description.

quote: The biological evaluation plan and report should follow the structure in ISO 10993-1 Annex A.
error: In ISO 10993-1:2018, which this flow cites as its edition at lines 795 and 804, Annex A is the table of biological endpoints to address (Table A.1). It does not set a structure for the biological evaluation plan or report. Guidance on carrying out the biological evaluation within the risk management process is in Annex B.
correct: ISO 10993-1:2018 Annex A (Table A.1) lists the biological endpoints to consider for each contact category and duration. Annex B gives guidance on conducting the biological evaluation within a risk management process, including planning and reporting.

quote: MRI labeling per ASTM F2503 is required for implantable devices
error: No regulation requires MRI labeling per ASTM F2503 for implantable devices. ASTM F2503 is an FDA-recognized consensus standard. FDA's guidance 'Testing and Labeling Medical Devices for Safety in the Magnetic Resonance (MR) Environment' (2023) recommends MR safety labeling for implants that may enter the MR environment. A recommendation is not a requirement.
correct: FDA recommends, through guidance, MR safety testing and labeling (MR Safe, MR Conditional or MR Unsafe, using the ASTM F2503 terms) for implants that may enter the MR environment. ASTM F2503 is a recognized standard, not a regulatory requirement.

quote: The primary endpoint must be met with statistical significance.
error: The string presents statistical significance on the primary endpoint as a requirement for PMA approval, and no regulation says that. FDA approves on reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness from valid scientific evidence (21 CFR 860.7; 814.45), weighing the totality of the evidence. Accepted designs include Bayesian designs and single-arm studies against an objective performance criterion, which this same flow offers as options. The flow's own check at line 1126 also says FDA weighs the totality of evidence.
correct: FDA decides whether the totality of valid scientific evidence gives reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness (21 CFR 860.7, 814.45). The pre-specified success criterion should be met. It is not a regulatory requirement that the primary endpoint reach frequentist statistical significance.

error: The reference for the 'Device Description Incomplete' finding cites 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(i). That paragraph is the summary's indications for use, not the device description. The finding's own requirement text on line 173 correctly names 814.20(b)(4)(i) for the complete description and 814.20(b)(3)(ii) for the summary device description.
correct: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4) for the complete device description, with its functional components, properties and principles of operation, and 814.20(b)(3)(ii) for the summary device description.

quote: FDA Guidance: Recommended Content and Format of Non-Clinical Bench Performance Testing Information in PMA Submissions
error: The guidance title is wrong. The FDA final guidance (2019) is titled '...in Premarket Submissions'. It covers 510(k)s, De Novos, PMAs, HDEs and IDEs, not PMAs only.
correct: FDA Guidance: Recommended Content and Format of Non-Clinical Bench Performance Testing Information in Premarket Submissions (December 2019)

quote: 21 CFR 801; FDA Guidance: Device Labeling Guidance (2018)
error: There is no 2018 CDRH guidance titled 'Device Labeling Guidance'. The closest FDA document with that name is the 1991 'Device Labeling Guidance' blue-book memorandum (#G91-1), so the citation names a document and year that do not exist as stated.
correct: Cite 21 CFR Part 801 and real labeling references, for example 'Labeling: Regulatory Requirements for Medical Devices' (FDA 89-4203) or 'Guidance on Medical Device Patient Labeling' (2001), or remove the guidance reference.

quote: 21 CFR 801.4; FDA Guidance: Device Labeling Guidance (2018)
error: This repeats the same non-existent 'Device Labeling Guidance (2018)' citation as line 151.
correct: Remove it or replace it with an existing labeling reference, for example 21 CFR Part 801 or 'Guidance on Medical Device Patient Labeling' (2001).

quote: FDA Form 3881; FDA Guidance: Device Labeling Guidance — Indications for Use Section
error: No FDA guidance with the title 'Device Labeling Guidance — Indications for Use Section' exists. The citation is fabricated.
correct: Cite FDA Form 3881 (Indications for Use) and, if a guidance is wanted, 'General/Specific Intended Use' (1998) or 'The 510(k) Program: Evaluating Substantial Equivalence in Premarket Notifications [510(k)]' (2014).

quote: A complete device description is required under 21 CFR 807.87(e), including sufficient detail for the reviewer to understand how the device works
error: 21 CFR 807.87(e) requires proposed labels, labeling and advertisements sufficient to describe the device, its intended use and its directions for use. It does not set a device-description requirement. The engineering and technical device description comes from 807.87(f), the comparison with similar devices and its supporting data, and from FDA's RTA/eSTAR content expectations. The same citation appears in the question on line 392 and the reference on line 406.
correct: Cite 21 CFR 807.87(f) together with the 510(k) RTA policy and eSTAR device-description content, not 807.87(e), which is the labeling paragraph.

error: ICH E6(R3) is cited as the GCP standard for a medical device pivotal investigation. ICH E6 covers clinical trials of investigational medicinal products (drugs and biologics). For device clinical investigations, FDA relies on 21 CFR 812/50/56 and the FDA-recognized device GCP standard, ISO 14155.
correct: 21 CFR 812; 21 CFR 50; 21 CFR 56; ISO 14155:2020 (Clinical investigation of medical devices for human subjects — Good clinical practice)

quote: reference: 'FD&C Act 513(f)(2)(A); 21 CFR 860.220(a)',
error: The finding cites 21 CFR 860.220(a) for the two conditions that make a device eligible for a De Novo request: a prior NSE determination, or no legally marketed predicate. 860.220 sets out what a De Novo request must contain; paragraph (a) covers administrative information. The eligibility conditions are in 21 CFR 860.200, 'Purpose and applicability', in Subpart D.
correct: FD&C Act 513(f)(2)(A); 21 CFR 860.200 (who may submit a De Novo request: after an NSE determination, or when there is no legally marketed predicate).

quote: This is a mandatory field and its absence will trigger an RTA (Refuse to Accept) determination.
error: Since 2023-10-01, 510(k) submissions to CDRH must be made through eSTAR. eSTAR submissions are not subject to the Refuse to Accept checklist review. FDA instead runs a technical screening, and an incomplete submission is put on hold. The eSTAR template also does not let a submission be built without the device name.
correct: In eSTAR the device name is a required field. A missing or incomplete element leads to a technical screening hold, not an RTA determination; RTA review does not apply to eSTAR 510(k)s.

quote: may result in an Additional Information (AI) request or Refuse to Accept (RTA) decision.
error: It names a Refuse to Accept decision as a possible outcome for a current 510(k). 510(k)s must now be submitted through eSTAR, and eSTAR submissions are not subject to RTA review.
correct: An inconsistency may lead to a technical screening hold, or to an Additional Information request during substantive review. RTA does not apply to eSTAR 510(k) submissions.

quote: is required per ISO 14971:2019 and ISO 13485:2016 Sections 7.1 and 7.3.7 (via 21 CFR 820.10, QMSR) as part of design validation.
error: ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3.7 (design and development validation) does not require risk analysis. Risk analysis as part of design validation was a requirement of the former QSR, 21 CFR 820.30(g), and was mapped onto 7.3.7 incorrectly. ISO 14971 also does not require FMEA or FTA specifically; ISO/TR 24971 describes those techniques as informative options.
correct: Risk management throughout product realization is required by ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.1 and is carried out per ISO 14971:2019 (via 21 CFR 820.10). Risk-management outputs feed design inputs (7.3.3). FMEA and FTA are recommended techniques, not mandated ones.

quote: FDA Guidance: Device Labeling Guidance (2018)
error: No FDA guidance called 'Device Labeling Guidance' was issued in 2018. The general device labeling guidance is the 1991 Device Labeling Guidance (#G91-1), supported by 'Labeling - Regulatory Requirements for Medical Devices' (1989). The same citation appears again at line 227.
correct: Cite 21 CFR Part 801 together with FDA's Device Labeling Guidance #G91-1 (1991), or with 'Labeling - Regulatory Requirements for Medical Devices' (FDA 89-4203).

quote: Devices with patient contact >24 hours require a comprehensive biocompatibility evaluation including systemic toxicity, genotoxicity, and (for implants) implantation and chronic toxicity testing per ISO 10993-1 Table A.1.
error: The statement says ISO 10993-1 Table A.1 requires systemic toxicity and genotoxicity for every device with more than 24 hours of contact. That is wrong. For surface devices on intact skin, Table A.1 lists only cytotoxicity, sensitization and irritation at every duration, including prolonged and permanent. Chronic toxicity is an endpoint only for long-term (permanent, more than 30 days) contact, so it is not called for in every implant with more than 24 hours of contact. The check fires as 'critical' on any prolonged or permanent contact, including intact-skin devices.
correct: ISO 10993-1:2018 Table A.1 sets the endpoints by both contact category and duration. Systemic toxicity and genotoxicity apply only to some categories with prolonged or permanent contact (for example breached surfaces, externally communicating devices and implants), not to intact-skin surface devices. Chronic toxicity applies to long-term contact.

quote: the routes are a De Novo request or a 510(k) for the new intended use.
error: A 510(k) cannot clear a new intended use. A device with a different intended use from its predicate is not substantially equivalent by definition (21 CFR 807.100(b); FD&C Act 513(i)). This text tells clients a 510(k) is a valid route for a new intended use, which contradicts the flow's own warning at line 424.
correct: If the indications and the technology come from different devices, the options are: a 510(k) on a single predicate (or several predicates, each with the same intended use) that has both the intended use and comparable technology, or a De Novo request (or a PMA) where no such predicate exists. A new intended use cannot be reached through a 510(k).

quote: 4th Edition (2014) — Required for new submissions
error: No edition of IEC 60601-1-2 is 'required' for new submissions. Conformance to a recognized consensus standard is voluntary. The edition FDA currently recognizes is also not the unamended 2014 4th edition: it is IEC 60601-1-2:2014+AMD1:2020 (Edition 4.1). The flow itself cites that version at line 613.
correct: FDA currently recognizes IEC 60601-1-2:2014+AMD1:2020 (Edition 4.1) and recommends it in its EMC guidance. Declaring conformity to it is a voluntary means of demonstrating EMC, not a requirement.

quote: clinical benefits (6), chemical properties (7), performance characteristics (8), design for safety (9)
error: Most of this description of MDR Annex I Chapter I is wrong. Risk management is GSPR 3, not GSPR 2. GSPR 6 covers performance over the device lifetime under normal conditions of use, not clinical benefits. GSPR 7 covers transport and storage, not chemical properties. GSPR 8 says known risks and side-effects are minimised and acceptable against benefits; it is not about performance characteristics. GSPR 9 covers Annex XVI products with no medical purpose, not design for safety.
correct: MDR Annex I Chapter I: 1 performance and safety; 2 reduce risks as far as possible; 3 risk management system; 4 risk control measures and information on residual risk; 5 use error and ergonomics; 6 performance and safety over the device lifetime; 7 transport and storage; 8 known risks and side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits; 9 Annex XVI products.

quote: GSPR 1 (safety/performance), 2 (risk management), 6 (clinical benefits), 8 (performance characteristics)
error: The wrong GSPR numbers are given as the ones usually needing clinical evidence. GSPR 6 is about lifetime performance, not clinical benefits. GSPR 8 is about side-effects and residual risks weighed against benefits, not performance characteristics. Risk management is GSPR 3, not GSPR 2.
correct: GSPR 1 (performance and safety), GSPR 8 (side-effects acceptable against benefits) and, where relevant, GSPRs 2-4 (risk reduction, risk management system, residual risk) and 6 (lifetime performance) are the ones usually supported by clinical data.

quote: chemical/physical/biological properties (10-11), infection (12), substances (13-14), software (15-17), active devices (18-22)
error: This misnumbers MDR Annex I Chapter II. Infection and microbial contamination is GSPR 11, not 12. GSPR 12 covers devices that incorporate a medicinal substance or are made of substances absorbed by the body. GSPR 13 covers materials of biological origin. GSPR 14 covers construction and interaction with the environment. GSPRs 15 and 16 cover diagnostic or measuring function and radiation, not software. Software is GSPR 17. GSPRs 20-22 (mechanical and thermal risks, energy or substance supply, lay-person devices) are not limited to active devices.
correct: 10 chemical, physical and biological properties; 11 infection and microbial contamination; 12 medicinal substances and absorbed substances; 13 materials of biological origin; 14 construction and interaction with the environment; 15 diagnostic and measuring function; 16 radiation; 17 electronic programmable systems and software; 18 active devices; 19 active implantable devices; 20 mechanical and thermal risks; 21 supply of energy or substances; 22 lay-person devices.

quote: provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(2)
error: Article 9(2) is the presumption of conformity for devices that meet a Common Specification. The rule that manufacturers must comply with a CS unless they justify an at-least-equivalent alternative is in Article 9(3).
correct: EU MDR Article 9(3).

quote: Labeling requirements including label, IFU, implant card per Annex I Section 23
error: The implant card is not an Annex I Section 23 requirement. Section 23 covers the label and the instructions for use. The implant card and the information supplied to implanted patients are set out in MDR Article 18.
correct: Label and IFU: MDR Annex I Section 23. Implant card: MDR Article 18.

quote: The CER must include a complete description of the device per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A1 is 'Demonstration of equivalence'; these same flow files cite it correctly for that elsewhere. The typical contents of a device description are in Appendix A3.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 (Device description – typical contents).

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: Appendix A1 covers demonstrating equivalence, not the device description.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1, the scope of the clinical evaluation is directly defined by the intended purpose.
error: Appendix A1 covers equivalence. The scope of the clinical evaluation (Stage 0) is MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7 (Definition of the scope of the clinical evaluation).

quote: the strictest classification prevails per Article 51(7)
error: Article 51 has no paragraph 7. The rule that the strictest applicable rule decides the class is in MDR Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5.
correct: EU MDR Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5.

quote: Per EU MDR Article 2(12), the intended purpose includes the medical condition, target patient population, and clinical benefits.
error: Article 2(12) defines intended purpose as the use for which a device is intended according to the manufacturer's label, IFU, promotional or sales materials and clinical evaluation. It does not list medical condition, patient population or clinical benefits. Those elements are required in the device description under Annex II Section 1.1.
correct: Article 2(12) defines intended purpose by the manufacturer's data. Indications, patient population and related elements are required by MDR Annex II Section 1.1.

quote: BSI 0086, TUV SUD 0123
error: 0086 is BSI's UK body, now a UK Approved Body under UKCA. It is not an EU MDR Notified Body and cannot certify CE marking under the MDR. BSI's EU MDR Notified Body is BSI Group The Netherlands, number 2797.
correct: e.g. BSI Group The Netherlands 2797, TÜV SÜD 0123.

quote: Under EU MDR Article 61(5), manufacturers demonstrating equivalence to a device of another manufacturer must have a contract in place
error: The Article 61(5) contract requirement applies only to implantable and Class III devices. For other classes, MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient access to the other manufacturer's data. It does not require a contract under Article 61(5). The same over-broad attribution to Article 61(5) appears at lines 163 and 184.
correct: Article 61(5): contract required for implantable and Class III devices claiming equivalence to another manufacturer's device. For all classes, Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient access to the equivalent device's data.

quote: MDCG 2020-5 provides guidance on clinical evaluation adequacy and the clinical data sets that should be considered.
error: MDCG 2020-5 is 'Clinical Evaluation – Equivalence: A guide for manufacturers and notified bodies'. It covers demonstrating equivalence, not clinical evaluation adequacy or which clinical data sets to consider.
correct: MDCG 2020-5 covers equivalence. Sufficiency of clinical evidence is covered by MDCG 2020-6, and data identification by MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.

quote: Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7, all data from the manufacturer's post-market surveillance system should be included.
error: Section 7 of MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 covers the scope of the clinical evaluation (Stage 0). Identifying pertinent data, including data generated and held by the manufacturer such as PMS data, is Section 8 (Stage 1, Section 8.1).
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1.

quote: This data feeds into the CER as clinical experience per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7.
error: Section 7 covers scope (Stage 0). Post-market and clinical-experience data held by the manufacturer is identified under Section 8 (Stage 1, Section 8.1).
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 8.1.

quote: ISO 14155:2020 Annex A provides guidance on literature search methodology for clinical investigations.
error: ISO 14155:2020 Annex A is the Clinical investigation plan (CIP). ISO 14155 has no annex on literature search methodology. The literature search and review protocol for a CER is in MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A5.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A5 (literature search and literature review protocol). ISO 14155:2020 Annex A is the CIP.

quote: Per EU MDR Article 61(11), CERs for implantable and Class III devices must be updated at least annually.
error: Article 61(11) requires the clinical evaluation to be updated throughout the device life cycle. For Class III and implantable devices, what it requires at least annually is the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP, not the CER. The same misattribution appears in the option label at line 149.
correct: Article 61(11): clinical evaluation updated throughout the life cycle. For Class III and implantable devices, the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP (Article 32) are updated at least annually.

quote: The CER must be reviewed and approved by the Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) per EU MDR Article 15
error: Article 15 does not require the PRRC to review or approve the CER. Article 15(3) makes the PRRC responsible for checking device conformity before release, keeping the technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity up to date, PMS obligations, vigilance reporting, and the clinical investigation statement.
correct: MDR Article 15(3) lists the PRRC's responsibilities, and CER approval is not among them. The CER is signed by the qualified clinical evaluators (MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 6.4).

quote: MDCG 2020-7 provides detailed guidance on PMCF plan and PMCF evaluation report content.
error: MDCG 2020-7 is the PMCF Plan template only. The PMCF Evaluation Report template is MDCG 2020-8, which the file itself cites at line 261.
correct: MDCG 2020-7: PMCF Plan template. MDCG 2020-8: PMCF Evaluation Report template.

quote: Required for interventional PMCF studies per EU MDR Article 70
error: Article 70 governs applications for pre-market clinical investigations. Under Article 74(1), a PMCF investigation that adds invasive or burdensome procedures needs a notification to the Member States at least 30 days before it starts. That route does not go through the Article 70 application procedure.
correct: EU MDR Article 74(1): notify the Member States concerned at least 30 days before starting.

quote: risk management (2), acceptability of benefit-risk (3-4), design for performance (5), clinical benefits (6), chemical properties (7), performance characteristics (8), design for safety (9)
error: This mapping of the Chapter I GSPRs is wrong. In MDR Annex I: GSPR 2 is reducing risk as far as possible; 3 is the risk management system; 4 is risk control measures; 5 is use error and ergonomics; 6 is that performance is kept over the device lifetime; 7 is transport and storage; 8 is that undesirable side-effects are minimised and acceptable; 9 is Annex XVI products. None of them is 'clinical benefits' or 'chemical properties'.
correct: 1 performance and safety; 2 risk reduction as far as possible; 3 risk management system; 4 risk control measures and information for safety; 5 use error and ergonomics; 6 characteristics kept during lifetime; 7 transport and storage; 8 side-effects minimised and acceptable against benefits; 9 Annex XVI products without a medical purpose.

quote: Typically includes GSPR 1 (safety/performance), 2 (risk management), 6 (clinical benefits), 8 (performance characteristics).
error: The GSPR numbers are given the wrong subjects. GSPR 2 is risk reduction as far as possible (risk management is GSPR 3). GSPR 6 is keeping performance over the device lifetime, not clinical benefits. GSPR 8 is minimising undesirable side-effects, not performance characteristics.
correct: The GSPRs that usually need clinical evidence are GSPR 1 (performance and safety, benefit-risk), GSPR 8 (undesirable side-effects acceptable against benefits) and, where relevant, GSPR 6 (lifetime). GSPR 2 is risk reduction as far as possible and GSPR 3 is risk management.

quote: Includes: chemical/physical/biological properties (10-11), infection (12), substances (13-14), software (15-17), active devices (18-22)
error: This mapping of the Chapter II GSPRs is wrong. GSPR 11 is infection and microbial contamination. GSPR 12 is devices incorporating a medicinal substance or made of absorbed substances. GSPR 13 is materials of biological origin. GSPR 14 is construction and interaction with the environment. GSPR 15 is diagnostic and measuring function. GSPR 16 is radiation. Software is GSPR 17 only. GSPRs 18-19 are active and active implantable devices. GSPRs 20-22 are mechanical and thermal risks, devices supplying energy or substances, and lay-person devices.
correct: 10 chemical/physical/biological properties; 11 infection and microbial contamination; 12 medicinal substances and absorbed substances; 13 biological origin; 14 construction and environment; 15 diagnostic and measuring function; 16 radiation; 17 software and electronic programmable systems; 18 active devices; 19 active implantable devices; 20 mechanical and thermal risks; 21 energy or substance delivery; 22 lay persons.

quote: provide justification that the alternative approach provides equivalent safety and performance per EU MDR Article 9(2)
error: The wrong paragraph is cited. Article 9(2) is the presumption of conformity for devices that conform to the CS. The duty to comply with CS unless an equivalent alternative is justified is in Article 9(3).
correct: EU MDR Article 9(3).

quote: all variants/models covered by this CER. Per MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section A1.
error: Appendix A1 covers demonstration of equivalence, not the device description.
correct: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3.

quote: Implantable as defined by EU MDR Article 2(5) — intended to be totally or partially introduced into the human body
error: This misstates the Article 2(5) definition. Being 'totally or partially introduced' alone describes any invasive device. Under Article 2(5), an implantable device must be introduced by surgical intervention and intended to remain in place after the procedure. A partially introduced device must be intended to remain for at least 30 days.
correct: Article 2(5): a device intended to be totally introduced into the body, or to replace an epithelial surface or the surface of the eye, by surgical intervention, and to remain after the procedure. A device partially introduced by surgical intervention counts only if it is intended to remain for at least 30 days.

quote: For devices where multiple rules apply, the strictest classification prevails per Article 51(7).
error: The 'strictest rule applies' principle is an implementing rule in Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5. Article 51 does not contain it.
correct: Annex VIII, Chapter II, Section 3.5: where several rules apply, the strictest rule, giving the higher class, applies.

quote: Name and NB number of the Notified Body (e.g. BSI 0086, TUV SUD 0123)
error: Since Brexit, BSI 0086 is a UK Approved Body and is not designated as an EU MDR Notified Body. BSI's EU MDR Notified Body is BSI Group The Netherlands B.V., number 2797.
correct: Give an EU-designated Notified Body as the example, e.g. BSI 2797 or TÜV SÜD 0123.

quote: An equivalent device must have the same clinical purpose, similar design, and use similar materials.
error: The biological criterion is wrong. MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 3 and MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 A1 require the SAME materials or substances in contact with the same human tissues or body fluids, not similar materials.
correct: Biologically, the device must use the same materials or substances in contact with the same human tissues or body fluids, for a similar kind and duration of contact.

quote: EU MDR Article 61(5) requires access to the equivalent device's technical documentation via contract when claiming equivalence to another manufacturer's device
error: The Article 61(5) contract requirement is limited to implantable and Class III devices. For other classes, Annex XIV Part A requires sufficient access to the data, not a contract.
correct: For implantable and Class III devices, Article 61(5) requires a contract giving full, ongoing access. For other classes, Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires sufficient levels of access to the data.

quote: Same clinical condition, same clinical purpose, same clinical effect, same site in body, same target population
error: Annex XIV Part A Section 3 requires a SIMILAR population (including age, anatomy and physiology), not the same population. It also requires the same kind of user and similar relevant critical performance, not the 'same clinical effect'.
correct: Same clinical condition or purpose (similar severity and stage of disease), same site in the body, similar population, same kind of user, and similar relevant critical performance for the expected clinical effect.

quote: Annual (required for Class III and implantable per Article 61(11))
error: Article 61(11) makes the annual update apply to the PMCF evaluation report and the SSCP, not the CER itself.
correct: Annual update of the PMCF evaluation report and SSCP is required for Class III and implantable devices (Article 61(11)). The CER is updated throughout the life cycle with that data.

quote: For Class III and implantable devices, a PMCF plan is always required.
error: The MDR does not exempt any class from the justification route. Annex III 1.1(b) and Annex XIV Part B allow, for any class, a PMCF plan or a justification of why PMCF is not applicable. A PMCF plan for Class III or implantable devices is an expectation, not an absolute legal rule.
correct: For all classes, including Class III and implantable devices, the MDR requires a PMCF plan or a justification of why PMCF is not applicable (Annex III 1.1(b)). For Class III and implantable devices that justification is rarely accepted.

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.4; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4; ISO/TR 24971 Clause 4.4'
error: MDR Annex II Section 4 covers the General Safety and Performance Requirements (applicable GSPRs, methods, standards, controlled documents). It does not cover risk management. The technical-documentation section on risk management is Annex II Section 5 ('Benefit-risk analysis and risk management').
correct: MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 5 (benefit-risk analysis and risk management, with reference to Annex I Sections 1, 3 and 8)

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 9; ISO/TR 24971 Clause 9; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4'
error: This cites Annex II Section 4 (GSPRs) for the risk management report. Risk management results belong to Annex II Section 5.
correct: MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 5

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4'
error: This cites Annex II Section 4 (GSPRs) for risk management traceability. Risk management documentation belongs to Annex II Section 5.
correct: MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 5

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 820.10
error: This cites Annex II Section 4 (GSPRs) for completeness of the risk management file. The risk management content of the technical documentation is Annex II Section 5.
correct: MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 5

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.1; ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5 (traceability); MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4'
error: This cites Annex II Section 4 (GSPR conformity) for tracing risk controls to hazards. Risk management results are Annex II Section 5. It also cites Clause 7.1 (risk control option analysis) as requiring implementation, but implementation is Clause 7.2.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 Clauses 7.1/7.2 and 4.5; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 5

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4; ISO/TR 24971 Annex A; IEC 60812 (FMEA); IEC 61025 (FTA)'
error: ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex A is 'Identification of hazards and characteristics related to safety'. Risk analysis techniques such as FMEA, FTA, HAZOP and HACCP are in Annex B ('Techniques that support risk analysis').
correct: ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex B

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4; IEC 60812; IEC 61025; ISO/TR 24971 Annex A'
error: This cites ISO/TR 24971 Annex A for structured failure-mode methods (FMEA, FTA). Those techniques are in Annex B. Annex A covers identification of hazards and characteristics related to safety.
correct: ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex B

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4; ISO/TR 24971 Annex A; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.1'
error: Causal-analysis techniques (e.g. FTA) are in ISO/TR 24971 Annex B, not Annex A. ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.1 is 'Responsibilities', not risk analysis or causal analysis; risk assessment is Section 4.3.
correct: ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex B; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.3 (Risk Assessment)

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.1 requires that risk control measures be implemented and verified.
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.1 is risk control option analysis. Implementation and verification of risk control measures (including effectiveness) are Clause 7.2.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.2 requires that the selected risk control measures be implemented and that their implementation and effectiveness be verified.

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.5; ISO/TR 24971 Clause 6.2'
error: ISO/TR 24971:2020 mirrors the clause structure of ISO 14971:2019. Its Clause 6 is risk evaluation, so a Clause 6.2/6.3 on severity or probability estimation does not exist. Risk estimation guidance is in Clause 5.5. The same mis-citation appears at line 248 ('ISO/TR 24971 Clause 6.3'), line 297 ('Clause 6.2') and lines 152/462 ('ISO/TR 24971 Clause 6' for risk estimation).
correct: ISO/TR 24971:2020 Clause 5.5 (risk estimation)

quote: recognized by FDA (via the RHTF)
error: FDA recognizes ISO 14971:2019 as a consensus standard through the CDRH Recognized Consensus Standards program (FD&C Act section 514(c)). No FDA mechanism called 'RHTF' exists.
correct: recognized by FDA as a consensus standard (FDA Recognized Consensus Standards database, under FD&C Act section 514(c))

quote: FDA Guidance: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices (2023)
error: The September 2023 final guidance 'Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions' was superseded by an updated final version issued in June 2025, so citing the 2023 version as current is out of date.
correct: FDA Guidance: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions (final, June 2025, superseding the September 2023 version)

quote: reference: 'MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 9; EU MDR Recital 1',
error: MDR Recital 1 says that Directives 90/385/EEC and 93/42/EEC need a fundamental revision. It says nothing about unmet clinical needs or the clinical context that justifies a device.
correct: Remove 'EU MDR Recital 1'. If an MDR anchor is wanted, Article 61(3)(c) / Annex XIV Part A Section 1 (consideration of currently available alternative treatment options and the state of the art) is the relevant provision.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.1 requires that risk control measures be implemented and verified.
error: In ISO 14971:2019, Clause 7.1 is risk control option analysis. Implementing risk control measures and verifying their implementation and effectiveness is Clause 7.2.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.2 requires that the selected risk control measures be implemented, and that their implementation and effectiveness be verified. Clause 7.1 covers selecting them through option analysis.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.3 requires evaluation of residual risk after each risk control is implemented, including assessment of whether new hazards or hazardous situations have been introduced.
error: Clause 7.3 (residual risk evaluation) does not cover new hazards. Checking whether risk control measures introduce new hazards or hazardous situations, or affect earlier risk estimates, is Clause 7.5 (risks arising from risk control measures).
correct: Clause 7.3 requires each residual risk to be evaluated against the acceptability criteria. Clause 7.5 requires review of whether risk control measures introduce new hazards or hazardous situations.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4 requires systematic techniques for hazard identification. ISO/TR 24971 recommends FMEA, FTA, HAZOP, or equivalent methods.
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4 requires the manufacturer to identify and document known and foreseeable hazards and hazardous situations. It does not require any particular technique, or FMEA/FTA/HAZOP-type techniques at all. ISO/TR 24971:2020 only describes such techniques as informative support, in Annex B ('Techniques that support risk analysis'), not in the Annex A cited here. The rule therefore treats a missing FMEA/FTA as a breach of a requirement that does not exist.
correct: Clause 5.4 requires identification of known and foreseeable hazards in normal and fault conditions, with no method mandated. ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex B describes optional techniques (PHA, FMEA, FTA, HAZOP, HACCP).

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4 requires systematic techniques for hazard identification. IEC 60812 provides a standardized methodology for FMEA.
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.4 does not require systematic techniques. It requires known and foreseeable hazards to be identified and documented, without prescribing a method.
correct: Clause 5.4 requires identification and documentation of known and foreseeable hazards and hazardous situations. FMEA (IEC 60812) is an optional technique, described in ISO/TR 24971 Annex B.

quote: 'ISO 14971:2019 Clause 5.5; ISO/TR 24971 Clause 6; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.3'
error: ISO/TR 24971:2020 uses the same clause numbering as ISO 14971:2019, so its guidance on risk estimation is in Clause 5.5 and Clause 6 is risk evaluation. Risk-estimation statements cite 'ISO/TR 24971 Clause 6' here and Clause 6, 6.2 or 6.3 at lines 225, 248, 297 and 462.
correct: Cite ISO/TR 24971:2020 Clause 5.5 (risk estimation) for severity and probability estimation. Clause 6 is risk evaluation.

quote: The file does not contain an overall benefit-risk analysis as required by ISO 14971:2019 Clause 8.
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 8 requires evaluation of the overall residual risk against the plan's criteria. A benefit-risk analysis is needed only when the overall residual risk is not judged acceptable, and then the manufacturer 'may' gather data to show that benefits outweigh it. The rule's own requirement text at line 432 says this correctly, so the question (and the title at line 420) state a requirement that does not exist.
correct: Clause 8 requires an evaluation of overall residual risk. A benefit-risk determination is needed under Clause 8 (and under Clause 7.4 for an individual risk) only when the residual risk is not acceptable under the criteria.

quote: EU MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 1 requires clear identification of the device, including trade name, model/size variants, and a precise statement of intended purpose.
error: MDR Annex XIV Part A Section 1 sets out what the clinical evaluation plan must contain: the applicable GSPRs, intended purpose, target groups, clinical benefits and so on. It does not require the trade name or model/size variants. Device identification by trade name and variants is a technical documentation requirement under Annex II Section 1.1.
correct: Annex XIV Part A Section 1(a) requires the clinical evaluation plan to specify the device's intended purpose and target groups. Identification by trade name and variants comes from Annex II Section 1.1 (and MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 for the CER's device description).

quote: reference: 'FDA Inspection Best Practices',
error: FDA has published no document called "FDA Inspection Best Practices". The reference points the client to a source that does not exist. No FDA regulation or guidance requires a mock-audit program or sets how often one is run.
correct: Remove the reference, or say plainly that mock audits are industry practice with no FDA citation. For internal-audit requirements, cite the real ones: ISO 13485:2016 §8.2.4 (internal audit, devices, via 21 CFR 820.10) and ICH Q10 (pharma).

quote: The risk management file must be complete before the risk management review. Ensure all required documents (risk management plan, risk analysis, risk evaluation, risk control records, residual risk evaluation, risk management report) are included.
error: This string says the risk management report must already be in the risk management file before the risk management review. Under ISO 14971:2019 clause 9, the report is the documented result of that review, so it cannot exist before the review. A file with no report is the normal state going into the review, not a gap.
correct: Before the clause 9 review, the file should contain the plan and the records of risk analysis, evaluation, control, residual-risk evaluation and overall residual-risk evaluation. Clause 9 then requires the results of the review to be documented as the risk management report and added to the risk management file.

quote: 21 CFR 211.192 requires that deviations be investigated commensurate with their significance.
error: 21 CFR 211.192 contains no proportionality or 'commensurate with significance' language. It requires that any unexplained discrepancy or failure to meet specifications be 'thoroughly investigated, whether or not the batch has already been distributed', with the investigation extended to other batches that may be affected. Risk-proportionate investigation depth comes from ICH Q9/Q10 thinking, not from the regulation. The same misattribution appears in the finding question at line 999.
correct: 21 CFR 211.192 requires that any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or its components to meet specifications be thoroughly investigated, with the investigation extended to other potentially affected batches and documented in writing. Scaling investigation depth to risk is an ICH Q9/Q10 principle.

quote: Per 21 CFR 211.188, every batch production and control record must be identifiable.
error: 21 CFR 211.188 covers batch production and control records: it requires one for each batch, with the listed contents. It does not govern SOP titles or SOP identification. Citing it as the basis for an SOP-title finding applies the wrong section. The same wording is repeated at line 67.
correct: Written procedures are required by 21 CFR 211.100(a), and document identification and control for devices falls under ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 via the QMSR. 211.188 applies only to batch records.

quote: requires that documents be available at locations of use and that obsolete documents be promptly removed
error: The words 'obsolete documents be promptly removed' come from the superseded QSR, former 21 CFR 820.40(a). ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 has no removal requirement. It requires the organization to prevent unintended use of obsolete documents and apply suitable identification to them. The same misattribution to 4.2.4 appears at line 745: 'Obsolete documents must be promptly removed from all points of use.'
correct: ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 requires that relevant versions of applicable documents be available at points of use, and that unintended use of obsolete documents be prevented and those documents suitably identified. 'Promptly removed' was the language of former 21 CFR 820.40(a), which no longer exists under the QMSR.

quote: The approved changes must be communicated to appropriate personnel in a timely manner.
error: This sentence continues a statement of what ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 requires, but it is the text of former 21 CFR 820.40(b) under the superseded QSR. ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 has no 'communicated in a timely manner' requirement.
correct: ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 requires that document changes be reviewed and approved by the original approving function or another designated function with access to pertinent background information, and that changes and current revision status be identified. The 'timely communication' wording was in former 21 CFR 820.40(b).

quote: requires that changes to documents be reviewed and approved by the same function/organization that performed the original review
error: ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 does not restrict change approval to the original function. It allows changes to be reviewed and approved either by the original approving function or by another designated function that has access to pertinent background information. The sentence that follows ('approved changes must be communicated to appropriate personnel in a timely manner') is wording from the old QSR 21 CFR 820.40(b), not from ISO 13485 clause 4.2.4.
correct: ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4: changes to documents are reviewed and approved either by the original approving function or by another designated function with access to pertinent background information on which to base its decisions.

quote: reference: 'ICH E2A Section III.B',
error: ICH E2A Section III.B is 'Reporting Time Frames': the 7-day and 15-day clocks and the minimum criteria for reporting. It does not set out the sponsor's duty to assess causality, which is what this check cites it for. Causality appears in E2A's definitions (II.A.1, 'reasonable causal relationship') and in III.A.1, which covers cases judged by the reporter or the sponsor to have a reasonable suspected causal relationship.
correct: Cite ICH E2A Section II.A.1 (ADR definition / reasonable causal relationship) and Section III.A.1 (cases where either the investigator or the sponsor suspects a causal relationship), not III.B.

quote: Per ICH E1, FDA expects at least 1,500 patients exposed for chronic-use drugs, with at least 300-600 exposed for 6 months and 100 for 12 months.
error: This misstates ICH E1. E1 is an ICH guideline, not a stand-alone FDA expectation. It applies only to long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, and it gives approximate figures: 'about 1500' in total and 300-600 for 6 months, not 'at least'. The first-pass correction at line 490 of the same file already states this scope limit. This helpText still states the old, overbroad version, so the two strings shown to the client contradict each other.
correct: Per ICH E1, for drugs intended for long-term (beyond 6 months) treatment of non-life-threatening conditions, the safety database is generally about 1,500 patients in total, 300-600 exposed for 6 months and at least 100 for 1 year; it does not apply to life-threatening indications.

quote: reference: 'PDUFA VI Commitment Letter; FDA Benefit-Risk Framework (2023)',
error: FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework does not date from 2023. FDA introduced it under PDUFA V (the 2013 'Structured Approach to Benefit-Risk Assessment in Drug Regulatory Decision-Making' plan), and the 2018 PDUFA VI implementation plan updated it. The 2023 document is a separate draft guidance, 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products' (September 2023), and it is not final. The guidance text at line 729 cites these documents correctly; this reference does not.
correct: PDUFA VI Commitment Letter; FDA 'Benefit-Risk Assessment in Drug Regulatory Decision-Making' (PDUFA VI implementation plan, 2018); FDA draft guidance 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products' (2023).

quote: placeholder: 'e.g., Division of Oncology Products 1, CDER',
error: CDER has not had a 'Division of Oncology Products 1' since the 2019-2020 reorganization of the Office of New Drugs. Oncology review divisions now sit in the Office of Oncologic Diseases, under names such as 'Division of Oncology 1'. The example shows clients a division name that no longer exists.
correct: e.g., Division of Oncology 1, Office of Oncologic Diseases, CDER

quote: FDA expects narratives to be included in IND annual reports (21 CFR 312.33)
error: 21 CFR 312.33 does not call for individual patient safety narratives. 312.33(b) asks for a narrative or tabular summary of the most frequent and most serious adverse experiences by body system, a summary of all IND safety reports, a list of deaths with cause, and a list of discontinuations due to adverse experiences. It is an aggregate summary, not case narratives.
correct: Individual case narratives go in CSR Section 12.3.2/14.3.3 (ICH E3) and the NDA/BLA safety summaries. The IND annual report (21 CFR 312.33(b)), or a DSUR filed in its place, holds aggregate narrative or tabular summaries of adverse experiences, a list of deaths and a list of discontinuations, not individual safety narratives.

quote: FDA typically publishes its own briefing document 1-2 business days before the meeting.
error: Under FDA's 2008 Advisory Committee guidance, FDA makes briefing materials public no later than 2 full business days before the meeting. Posting 1 business day before would fall short of that. This line also contradicts line 76 of the same flow ('at least two business days before the meeting').
correct: FDA posts its briefing document, and the sponsor's, publicly no later than 2 business days before the meeting. In practice this is usually exactly 2 business days.

quote: reference: 'FDAAA §505-1; FDA REMS Guidance (2022)',
error: Section 505-1 belongs to the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 355-1), not to FDAAA. FDAAA (Pub. L. 110-85) added it through FDAAA §901, and FDAAA has no section 505-1 of its own.
correct: FD&C Act §505-1 (21 U.S.C. 355-1), added by FDAAA §901 (2007).

quote: FDA Guidance on Expedited Programs (2014, updated 2023)
error: FDA's 'Expedited Programs for Serious Conditions — Drugs and Biologics' guidance was finalised in May 2014 and was not updated in 2023. The later accelerated-approval documents are separate drafts: the oncology-specific 'Clinical Trial Considerations to Support Accelerated Approval of Oncology Therapeutics' (March 2023), 'Expedited Program for Serious Conditions — Accelerated Approval of Drugs and Biologics' (December 2024), and the confirmatory-trial-underway draft (January 2025).
correct: FDA Guidance 'Expedited Programs for Serious Conditions — Drugs and Biologics' (final, May 2014), plus the separate draft guidance 'Expedited Program for Serious Conditions — Accelerated Approval of Drugs and Biologics' (December 2024).

quote: reference: 'FDORA §3210; 21 CFR 314.530;
error: This rule fires for bla_submission too, but 21 CFR 314.530 is the withdrawal procedure for drugs approved under accelerated approval (Part 314 subpart H, NDAs). For biologics the counterpart is 21 CFR 601.43 (Part 601 subpart E), so a BLA sponsor is pointed to a regulation that does not govern their product.
correct: 21 CFR 314.530 for NDAs; 21 CFR 601.43 for BLAs (accelerated approval withdrawal procedures).

quote: Draft the ICH E3 §16 patient safety narrative
error: ICH E3 puts patient narratives of deaths, other serious adverse events and certain other significant adverse events in section 12.3.2, which says they may go in the report text or in section 14.3.3. Section 16 holds the appendices: 16.2.7 is the per-patient adverse event listings, not the narratives.
correct: ICH E3 §12.3.2 / §14.3.3 (narratives of deaths, other serious and certain other significant adverse events).

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance on Rare Disease Drug Development (2019); Orphan Drug Act §526',
error: Two errors. (1) Section 526 is an FD&C Act section (21 U.S.C. 360bb, orphan designation); the Orphan Drug Act of 1983 added it to the FD&C Act but does not number it §526. (2) The 2019 rare-disease guidance ('Rare Diseases: Common Issues in Drug Development') was a revised draft, and FDA replaced it with the final 'Rare Diseases: Considerations for the Development of Drugs and Biological Products' (December 2023). Citing the 2019 draft as current is wrong. For natural history specifically, the relevant guidance is 'Rare Diseases: Natural History Studies for Drug Development' (2019).
correct: FD&C Act §526 (21 U.S.C. 360bb), as added by the Orphan Drug Act; FDA Guidance 'Rare Diseases: Considerations for the Development of Drugs and Biological Products' (final, December 2023); 'Rare Diseases: Natural History Studies for Drug Development' (2019).

quote: `${agencyFor('EU')} has no part in them, beyond the companion-diagnostic consultation.`
error: This sentence is shown for both MDR and IVDR route lists. Under the MDR, EMA's role is not a companion-diagnostic consultation (that one is IVDR-only, Art 48 / Annex IX §5.2). Under the MDR, EMA (or a national medicines authority) is consulted on devices that incorporate an ancillary medicinal substance, human blood or plasma derivatives, and Rule 21 systemically absorbed substances (MDR Annex IX §5.2). The line 81 claim that 'a notified body assesses them' is also wrong for self-declared routes: MDR Class I that is not sterile, measuring or reusable surgical, and IVDR Class A that is not sterile. The IVDR list on the same page labels Class A 'no notified body'.
correct: For MDR: the notified body assesses Class Is/Im/Ir, IIa, IIb and III; plain Class I is self-declared; EMA or a national competent authority is consulted for devices with an ancillary medicinal substance (MDR Annex IX §5.2). For IVDR: Class A non-sterile is self-declared; EMA or a national competent authority is consulted for companion diagnostics (IVDR Art 48(3)/(4), Annex IX §5.2).

quote: ICH Q1E limits extrapolation to 2x the period covered by long-term data.
error: This misstates the ICH Q1E limit. Twice the long-term period is the most Q1E allows, and only in the best case (room-temperature storage, little or no change, statistics where applicable). Even then the cap is "up to twice, but not more than 12 months beyond" the long-term data. Refrigerated products, and products where data are amenable to statistics but none was done, are limited to 1.5x and no more than 6 months beyond. As written, the finding treats a 48-month shelf life on 24 months of data as within the limit, but Q1E caps it at 36 months.
correct: ICH Q1E allows extrapolation of up to twice the long-term period, but no more than 12 months beyond it, and only where the data support it (little or no change, statistical analysis where applicable, room-temperature storage). In other cases the limit is 1.5x and no more than 6 months beyond, and refrigerated products are limited further.

quote: If a REMS is required, the Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) must be clearly defined.
error: Not every REMS includes ETASU. Under FD&C Act 505-1, a REMS can consist only of a Medication Guide, a patient package insert and/or a communication plan. ETASU (505-1(f)) are required only when FDA decides those other elements are not enough to mitigate a specific serious risk. Saying any REMS must define ETASU states as a requirement something that is not one.
correct: A REMS may consist of a Medication Guide, a patient package insert and/or a communication plan. ETASU are required only when FDA determines they are needed (FD&C Act 505-1(f)). If the REMS includes ETASU, they must be specified, together with an implementation system where required.

quote: has no part in them, beyond the companion-diagnostic consultation.
error: This text is shown for MDR (medical device) routes as well as IVDR routes. Companion-diagnostic consultation happens under the IVDR (Annex IX §5.2 / Art 48(3)-(4)), not under the MDR. Under the MDR, EMA or a national medicines authority is consulted by the notified body for devices that incorporate an ancillary medicinal substance (MDR Annex IX §5.2, Rule 14). EMA consultation is mandatory for substances derived from human blood or plasma, and for medicines within centralised-procedure scope. Systemically absorbed substance-based devices (Rule 21, Annex IX §5.4) also involve a medicines authority. So for MDR the sentence is wrong.
correct: For MDR routes: a notified body assesses them, and EMA or a national medicines authority is consulted for devices that incorporate an ancillary medicinal substance (Annex IX §5.2) and for Rule 21 substance-based devices. Companion-diagnostic consultation with EMA or a national authority is an IVDR feature.

quote: FDA and EMA both expect an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) for studies involving children.
error: Neither FDA nor EMA expects an independent DSMB for every pediatric study. FDA's DMC guidance and EMA's DMC guideline treat a vulnerable population, children included, as one factor in a risk-based decision on whether a DMC is warranted. Most pediatric PK or short low-risk studies run without one. The finding is CRITICAL and presents a case-by-case consideration as a blanket requirement.
correct: For studies in children, FDA (DMC guidance) and EMA (Guideline on Data Monitoring Committees) say an independent DMC/DSMB should be considered. Pediatric status is one factor, alongside trial risk, endpoints such as mortality or serious morbidity, and duration. It is not a universal expectation.

quote: Draft the ICH E3 §16 patient safety narrative from the collected case facts
error: ICH E3 does not put patient safety narratives in section 16. Section 16 holds the appendices, for example 16.2.7 adverse event listings and 16.3 CRFs. E3 places narratives of deaths, other serious AEs and certain other significant AEs in section 12.3.2 or section 14.3.3.
correct: Patient safety narratives per ICH E3 §12.3.2, placed in §12.3.2 or §14.3.3.
